Prose containing the word 'undefined' (e.g. in a project description) triggers the same false failure.
findings.suggestion: Strip <script>...</script> bodies (except checking rendered text nodes) before running the regex, or narrow it to interpolation-shaped leaks such as />\s*undefined\s*</, ">undefined<", '="undefined"' patterns.
findings.verifyNote: Line 32 does run the bare /\b(undefined|NaN)\b/ regex over the whole HTML including inline scripts, so the false-positive risk is real for is:inline scripts and prose; however processed component scripts are minified (undefined → void 0, as BootIntro.astro proves), the check passes today, and blanket strictness in a leak detector is a design tradeoff rather than a confirmed defect.

findings.summary: A bare href="#" (hash-only, common back-to-top idiom) would fail with a confusing 'internal link # has no matching target' error.
findings.detail: For target '#', slice(1) yields '' and idSet.has('') is false, so the script reports a broken internal link. No such href exists in dist today, but it is a latent trap: adding a conventional `href="#"` top-of-page link or a placeholder anchor would break the release gate with a message that does not explain the real rule.
findings.suggestion: Handle `target === "#"` explicitly — either allow it or emit a dedicated message ('use href="#main" instead of bare #') so the failure is actionable.
findings.verifyNote: scripts/check-build.mjs:40 behaves exactly as claimed (href="#" would fail with a confusing message), but no such href exists today, so it is a latent ergonomics concern rather than a current defect.

findings.summary: Local-asset validation silently skips relative hrefs/srcs and absolute URLs to the site's own domain, so those broken links false-pass.
findings.detail: Line 43 `if (!target.startsWith("/") || target.startsWith("//")) continue;` skips every target that is not root-relative. That correctly skips mailto:/https:// external links, but it also skips (a) document-relative paths like `assets/foo.png` that an author could introduce, and (b) absolute URLs to the site itself — dist/index.html already contains `href="https://ramuroy.github.io/"`, and a typo'd own-domain URL like `https://ramuroy.github.io/resume.pdf` would never be checked against dist. The script's stated purpose (validate all local links) is therefore not fully met.
findings.suggestion: Before the startsWith('/') test, rewrite targets beginning with `https://ramuroy.github.io` (import the site constant) to their pathname and validate them; also flag or validate document-relative targets instead of skipping them.
findings.verifyNote: Premise verified at scripts/check-build.mjs:43 — relative and own-domain absolute targets are indeed skipped and dist/index.html contains href="https://ramuroy.github.io/" — but no link is actually broken today, so whether the validator should cover these hypothetical cases is a scope judgment call.

findings.summary: Fragments on path-form internal links (e.g. /#projects) are never validated — only bare #fragment hrefs are checked against the ID set.
findings.detail: Line 40 handles targets starting with '#', but a link written as `/#projects` or `/index.html#does-not-exist` takes the file-existence branch: `new URL(target, base).pathname` drops the fragment, dist/index.html exists, and the check passes even though the anchor target may be missing. This is a realistic authoring style for a single-page site and would false-pass a broken section link.
findings.suggestion: Extract `url.hash` in the local-asset branch and, when the resolved file is dist/index.html, verify `idSet.has(url.hash.slice(1))` just like the bare-fragment branch.
findings.verifyNote: scripts/check-build.mjs:45 — `new URL(target, base).pathname` drops the fragment, so path-form links like `/#projects` skip the idSet check on line 40 and only get a file-existence test; no other code validates such fragments.

findings.summary: tsconfig extends astro/tsconfigs/strict rather than strictest, leaving useful checks (noUncheckedIndexedAccess, noImplicitReturns, noUnusedLocals, etc.) off.
findings.detail: Astro ships a 'strictest' preset intended for exactly this kind of small greenfield codebase; the hardening docs emphasize maximal static guarantees, and `astro check` is already the first stage of the release gate, so the stricter preset is cheap to adopt now and expensive later.
findings.suggestion: Change extends to "astro/tsconfigs/strictest" and fix any resulting diagnostics.
findings.verifyNote: tsconfig.json:2 does extend astro/tsconfigs/strict and the installed strictest preset would add the cited flags, but switching presets is a stylistic/policy judgment rather than a factual defect.

findings.summary: No .editorconfig to normalize indentation, charset, and final-newline behavior across editors.
findings.detail: The repo mixes .astro, .ts, .css, .mjs, .yml, and .md files with hand-maintained formatting and no formatter enforcement (see the missing-prettier finding); an .editorconfig is the zero-dependency baseline that keeps contributors' editors consistent.
findings.suggestion: Add a root .editorconfig (root=true, utf-8, lf, insert_final_newline=true, indent_style=space, indent_size=2).
findings.verifyNote: Factual premise verified — no .editorconfig or any formatter config exists in /home/sena/ESPworkspace/ramuroy.github.io — but adding one is a discretionary tooling-hygiene suggestion, not a concrete defect.

findings.summary: No timeout-minutes on either job and checkout does not set persist-credentials: false.
findings.detail: Both jobs default to the 360-minute job timeout, so a hung npm install or deploy burns runner minutes for 6 hours. actions/checkout also persists the GITHUB_TOKEN into .git/config by default, exposing it to the npm scripts run during `npm ci` (token is read-only for contents here, so impact is low).
findings.suggestion: Add `timeout-minutes: 10` to the build job and `timeout-minutes: 5` to the deploy job, and set `with: persist-credentials: false` on the checkout step.
findings.verifyNote: deploy.yml has no timeout-minutes on either job and checkout@v4 uses default persist-credentials: true; impact is low since permissions grant only contents: read, exactly as the finding states.

findings.summary: .gitignore covers .env and .env.production but not .env.development or .env.local variants.
findings.detail: Lines 13-14 ignore only two specific env filenames. Astro/Vite also read .env.development, .env.local, and .env.[mode].local; a contributor creating .env.development with a secret would not be ignored (the `*.local` pattern on line 17 does catch .env.local, but not .env.development).
findings.suggestion: Replace the two entries with a `.env*` pattern (optionally re-including a committed `.env.example` via `!.env.example`).
findings.verifyNote: .gitignore lines 13-14 ignore only .env and .env.production; *.local (line 17) covers .env.local variants but .env.development is genuinely unignored — a real, if minor, gap as claimed.

findings.summary: Three config options restate Astro defaults: trailingSlash: 'ignore', build.inlineStylesheets: 'auto', and compressHTML: true.
findings.detail: All three values (lines 10, 33-35, 36) are the documented Astro defaults, so they add noise without changing behavior, and pinning defaults can mask intentional upstream default changes across major versions. The sitemap() integration is also called with no options; for a single-page site adding lastmod would give crawlers real signal, since dist/sitemap-0.xml currently contains only a bare <loc>.
findings.suggestion: Remove the redundant default-value options (or comment that they are deliberate pins), and consider `sitemap({ lastmod: new Date() })` or a fixed content date.
findings.verifyNote: All three options at astro.config.mjs:10, 33-35, 36 do restate Astro defaults and sitemap-0.xml has only a bare <loc>, but removing redundant defaults vs. keeping them as explicit pins is a stylistic judgment call with no behavioral impact.

findings.summary: packageManager: npm@10.8.2 is inert and slightly inconsistent — corepack is not enabled in CI and Node 22.12.0 bundles npm 10.9.x.
findings.detail: The packageManager field only takes effect via corepack, which neither the workflow nor the README enables; CI actually runs the npm bundled with Node 22.12.0 (10.9.0), not 10.8.2. README says 'the intended package manager is recorded in package.json', but the recorded version is never the one used, so the pin gives false precision.
findings.suggestion: Either enable corepack in CI/docs (`corepack enable` before npm ci) to make the pin real, or change the field to the npm version actually shipped with the pinned Node (npm@10.9.0), or drop the patch pin.
findings.verifyNote: package.json:6 pins packageManager npm@10.8.2 but deploy.yml never enables corepack (Node 22.12.0 setup runs its bundled npm 10.9.0), and README:26 points to the never-honored pin — the inconsistency is real, though severity is correctly just polish.

findings.summary: The id-extraction regex /\bid="([^"]+)"/ over-matches: it captures data-id/aria-*id attributes and id= strings inside inline scripts/JSON-LD.
findings.detail: Because '-' is a non-word character, \b matches inside `data-id="x"` and similar suffixed attributes, and the regex also runs over inline <script> bodies, so a JS string containing `id="main"` would both inflate the duplicate-ID count and satisfy required-ID checks without the element existing in the DOM. No such content exists in the current build, but the validator is regex-over-HTML and will drift as components change.
findings.suggestion: Use a negative lookbehind (/(?<![-\w])id="([^"]+)"/) and strip <script> elements from the HTML before scanning, or parse with a small HTML parser (e.g. node:html via linkedom/parse5) since this script already gates releases.
findings.verifyNote: Premise verified: at scripts/check-build.mjs:20 the regex /\bid="([^"]+)"/g does match `data-id="a"` (word boundary after '-') and `id="main"` inside script-body strings (empirically tested in node), but the current dist/index.html contains only 9 plain `id="` attributes and no data-id/script false positives, so this is latent robustness polish rather than a live defect — a judgment call, as the finding itself concedes.

findings.summary: Several checks depend on exact attribute ordering/serialization (canonical link, <html lang>, main landmark, JSON-LD script tag) and will false-fail if Astro reorders attributes.
findings.detail: Lines 25-30 and 56 use exact-substring matches like `rel="canonical" href="https://ramuroy.github.io/"` and `<script type="application/ld+json">`. These pass against the current compressHTML output, but any attribute added or reordered by a future Astro version (e.g. `data-astro-*`, or `<html lang="en" dir="ltr">`) breaks the gate even though the page is semantically correct.
findings.suggestion: Match attributes independently (e.g. find the <link> tag containing both rel="canonical" and the href, in either order) or parse the HTML instead of substring matching.
findings.verifyNote: Premise verified — lines 25-27 and 56 of scripts/check-build.mjs do use order-sensitive exact-substring matches with no looser fallback — but the checks currently pass and the brittleness only bites under hypothetical future Astro serialization changes, making it a polish/judgment call rather than a present defect.

findings.summary: og:image is only checked for presence, not that its content is an absolute URL pointing at an existing asset.
findings.detail: Line 29 checks `property="og:image"` exists and line 76 checks dist/og.png exists, but nothing ties them together: an og:image content of a relative path (invalid per the OG spec) or a typo'd filename would still pass both checks.
findings.suggestion: Extract the og:image content attribute, assert it starts with 'https://ramuroy.github.io/', and assert the referenced file exists in dist.
findings.verifyNote: scripts/check-build.mjs:29 only tests for the substring property="og:image"; the href/src asset loop at line 38 skips meta content attributes, so a relative or typo'd og:image URL passes while dist/og.png is checked independently at line 76.

findings.summary: existsSync asset checks are case-insensitive on macOS/Windows dev machines, so a case-mismatched asset reference can pass locally and 404 on GitHub Pages.
findings.detail: GitHub Pages serves case-sensitively; `existsSync(join(dist, 'ramu_roy_resume.pdf'))` would return true on a default APFS/NTFS volume while the deployed URL 404s. This is fully mitigated pre-deploy because CI runs the same check on ubuntu-latest, but a developer relying on local `npm run verify` gets a false pass.
findings.suggestion: After existsSync succeeds, confirm the exact-case entry appears in readdirSync(dirname(localPath)) so the check is case-exact on every OS.
findings.verifyNote: Premise is accurate — scripts/check-build.mjs:48 (and 76-78) use plain existsSync with no case-exact guard, so macOS/Windows local runs can false-pass a case-mismatched asset — but deploy.yml runs the same check on ubuntu-latest before publishing, so the impact is limited to local dev ergonomics, making the fix a judgment-call polish item.

findings.summary: target="_blank" tag regex [^>]* breaks on '>' inside attribute values, and links whose target attribute uses single quotes or no target at all are unexamined.
findings.detail: `/<a\b[^>]*target="_blank"[^>]*>/g` truncates the tag at the first '>' character even inside a quoted attribute value (e.g. aria-label="A > B"), which would make the rel= lookup miss and report a false noopener failure — or, truncated the other way, skip the tag entirely. All 16 current _blank links pass, but the regex is fragile against ordinary content.
findings.suggestion: Match tags with a quote-aware pattern (/<a\b(?:[^>"']|"[^"]*"|'[^']*')*>/g) and then test for target="_blank" and rel within each captured tag.
findings.verifyNote: The regex at scripts/check-build.mjs:51 truncates/skips tags containing '>' in attribute values exactly as described, but all 16 current _blank links pass and Astro output never triggers the edge case, so it is a latent robustness concern rather than a present bug.

findings.summary: The include and exclude entries duplicate what astro/tsconfigs/base.json already declares via ${configDir}.
findings.detail: node_modules/astro/tsconfigs/base.json (extended through strict.json) already sets `"exclude": ["${configDir}/dist"]` and `"include": ["${configDir}/.astro/types.d.ts", "${configDir}/**/*"]`, which resolve to the project directory. The local copies at lines 3-4 override the base with identical values — harmless today, but they will mask future upstream changes to the Astro preset.
findings.suggestion: Delete the local include/exclude entries and rely on the inherited ${configDir}-based values, or add a comment explaining why they are pinned locally.
findings.verifyNote: Factual premise verified — tsconfig.json:3-4 duplicate the ${configDir}-based include/exclude inherited from astro/tsconfigs/base.json — but removing them is a stylistic judgment call (Astro's own starter templates ship these exact lines), with no functional impact today.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus indicators disappear entirely in Windows High Contrast / forced-colors mode because the only focus style is outline:none + box-shadow.
findings.detail: The single global focus rule is `:where(a, button, input, [tabindex]):focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--focus-ring); ... }` — the only `outline` declaration in the whole stylesheet. In forced-colors mode (Windows High Contrast, Edge/Chrome/Firefox) box-shadow is forced to none, and outline:none removes the UA default, so every link, button, and the skip link has no visible focus indicator at all. There is no @media (forced-colors: active) block anywhere in src/styles (grep confirms zero occurrences), so the mode also silently erases the gauge fills (background gradient), LED/status dots (background), and the .link / .nav__link underline affordances (background-image / ::after background). The forced-colors user state was never tested by any auditor.
findings.suggestion: Use a transparent outline that forced-colors can repaint: replace outline:none with `outline: 2px solid transparent; outline-offset: 2px;` (keeping the box-shadow ring for normal mode), and add an @media (forced-colors: active) block giving gauges/dots/underlines border- or currentColor-based fallbacks.
findings.verifyNote: global.css:135 is the only outline declaration in src (grep confirms), no forced-colors media query exists anywhere, and forced-colors mode suppresses box-shadow while honoring outline:none — so focus indicators do vanish for High Contrast users exactly as claimed.

findings.summary: Without JavaScript the mobile nav menu can never be opened: nav links are unreachable at <=720px, violating the site's stated no-JS hard requirement.
findings.detail: Under @media (max-width: 720px), .nav__links is set to opacity:0; pointer-events:none; visibility:hidden and is only revealed by the [data-open] attribute, which is toggled exclusively by JS in Layout.astro (navList?.toggleAttribute("data-open")). The .nav__menu-btn is shown by pure CSS (no .js gating), so no-JS mobile users see a menu button that does nothing and have zero access to the About/Projects/Experience/Skills/Contact/GitHub links. This directly contradicts README.md line 83-85 ("content must remain visible and usable if JavaScript ... unavailable") and docs/architecture.md ("it is not required to read the content or follow the primary links"). The same dead-button state also occurs on slow connections until the deferred Layout module loads. No auditor flagged the no-JS path; only the 721-820px overflow was reported.
findings.suggestion: Provide a CSS-only fallback: gate the hidden state behind .js (e.g. .js .nav__links { ... }) so no-JS users get an always-visible link list, or implement the menu with a <details>/popover element that works natively; alternatively hide .nav__menu-btn when html:not(.js).
findings.verifyNote: global.css:223 hides .nav__links at <=720px with no .js gating and the only reveal is the JS-toggled [data-open] attribute (Layout.astro:227); Nav.astro uses a plain button/ul with no native fallback, so no-JS mobile users cannot open the nav, violating the README lines 83-85 progressive-enhancement contract.

findings.summary: The boot overlay is an aria-modal dialog with no focus containment: Tab moves focus into the invisible page behind the opaque overlay, and Escape only works while focus stays inside the dialog.
findings.detail: The overlay is role="dialog" aria-modal="true" and focuses .boot__skip, but nothing traps Tab: the next Tab lands on .skip-link, which is z-index 200 and rendered *under* the z-index 300 opaque .boot layer, so a keyboard user is focused on an element they cannot see; further Tabs walk the whole hidden page (body overflow:hidden only stops scrolling, not focus). The Escape handler is attached to the boot element itself (line 70), so once focus has escaped the dialog, Escape no longer dismisses it. Additionally the entire visible content (.boot__panel) is aria-hidden="true", so screen-reader users experience an unexplained modal containing only a "skip intro" button. aria-modal claims background inertness that is not actually implemented.
findings.suggestion: While the boot is active, set the inert attribute on .skip-link, .nav, main and footer (removing it on dismiss), move the Escape listener to document, and either un-hide the boot lines or give the dialog a description so aria-modal semantics match reality.
findings.verifyNote: Verified: aria-modal dialog at BootIntro.astro:4 has no focus trap or inert siblings, Escape listener is scoped to the boot element (line 70), .boot__panel is aria-hidden (line 6), and .skip-link (z-index 200) sits under the opaque z-index-300 overlay per global.css:69/236; the 1300 ms auto-dismiss merely limits exposure, matching the minor severity.

findings.summary: The two "copy" buttons render and are focusable without JavaScript but do nothing — a dead interactive control in the no-JS baseline.
findings.detail: The copy-btn <button> elements are server-rendered unconditionally; their only behavior comes from the deferred [data-copy] listener in Layout.astro. With JS disabled (or before the module loads on a slow connection), keyboard and screen-reader users encounter focusable buttons labelled "Copy email"/"Copy phone number" that silently do nothing when activated. Every other enhancement on the page (boot, reveals, counters) was made fail-open per docs/decisions.md D-006, but this one was missed.
findings.suggestion: Hide the buttons by default and reveal them via the existing html.js hook (e.g. `.copy-btn { display: none } .js .copy-btn { display: inline-flex }`), or inject the buttons from the script that wires them.
findings.verifyNote: Contact.astro:21/28 render the copy buttons unconditionally, their only behavior is the deferred [data-copy] listener in Layout.astro:198, and no CSS (.js gating) or noscript rule hides them without JS — while other enhancements like .reveal are .js-gated in global.css:97.

findings.summary: aria-hidden separator dots make the protocols line and hero ticker read as one concatenated word to screen readers ("UARTSPII²CCAN…", "cgpa 8.3esp-idf v5.2yocto…").
findings.detail: Both the protocols line (`{i > 0 && ·}{p}`) and the hero ticker in Hero.astro line 40 hide the only separator between items with aria-hidden, and compressHTML leaves no whitespace between the items in the built HTML (`UART·SPI` — verified in dist/index.html). The accessibility tree therefore contains the items butted directly together with no boundary, so screen readers announce them as run-together nonsense words. Copy-paste of the line has the same defect.
findings.suggestion:
Keep the visual dot but make the semantic boundary real: render the lists as
    with visually-styled separators, or put a visually-hidden comma/space (e.g. , ) between items instead of aria-hiding the only delimiter.
findings.verifyNote: Verified in source (Skills.astro:27, Hero.astro:40) and built dist/index.html: the only separator between items is aria-hidden and compressHTML leaves no whitespace, so the accessibility tree concatenates the items; nothing elsewhere mitigates it (minor caveat: copy-paste does retain the dot, just no spaces).

findings.summary: Personal mobile number (and email) are published in machine-readable JSON-LD and plaintext HTML with zero obfuscation, maximizing spam/scraper harvesting.
findings.detail: The Person JSON-LD includes telephone: "+91 94936 52315" and email: "mailto:royramu694429@gmail.com"; the same phone appears as a tel: link plus data-copy attribute in Contact.astro, and the email appears in three mailto: hrefs. Structured data is specifically what bulk harvesters and SEO scrapers parse first, and Google can surface the phone number in knowledge panels. For a personal (not business) mobile number on a public site this is a meaningful privacy/spam exposure the privacy dimension never assessed. No other auditor covered the explicitly-requested email-obfuscation/harvesting angle.
findings.suggestion: Confirm the owner genuinely wants the personal mobile number crawlable; at minimum drop `telephone` from the JSON-LD Person block, and consider rendering the phone only behind the copy interaction or as an image/JS-assembled string while keeping the visible text for humans.
findings.verifyNote: Factual premise fully verified — telephone/email in JSON-LD at Layout.astro:22-23, tel: link + data-copy in Contact.astro:27-28, three mailto: hrefs, zero obfuscation — but whether crawlable contact info on a personal portfolio's contact page is a defect is an owner-intent judgment call, not an objective bug.

findings.summary: Double-clicking a copy button permanently sticks it on "copied ✓" (and aria-label "Copied") because the restore timeout captures the already-swapped text.
findings.detail: The click handler does `const prev = btn.textContent; btn.textContent = "copied ✓"; setTimeout(() => { btn.textContent = prev; ... }, 1400)` without clearing any pending timeout. Click twice within 1400ms: the second click captures prev="copied ✓" and prevLabel="Copied"; the first timeout restores "copy", then the second timeout fires and sets the text back to "copied ✓" and aria-label to "Copied" — and every subsequent click now captures the wrong values, so the button label and accessible name are wrong for the rest of the session. Concrete repro: on /#contact, click the email "copy" button twice quickly; after 3 seconds the button still reads "copied ✓".
findings.suggestion: Store the pristine label once (e.g. data-original-label at setup or a per-button WeakMap), clear the previous timeout with clearTimeout before starting a new one, and always restore from the stored original rather than the live textContent.
findings.verifyNote: Layout.astro:205-215 captures prev from live textContent with no clearTimeout or stored original label, so a second click within 1400ms leaves the button stuck on "copied ✓"/aria-label "Copied" exactly as described.

findings.summary: @font-face src URLs reach into node_modules internals via relative paths (../../node_modules/@fontsource-variable/...), bypassing the packages' public exports and coupling the build to npm's physical layout.
findings.detail: All three font declarations hardcode `url("../../node_modules/@fontsource-variable/<pkg>/files/<file>.woff2")`. This works only because Vite happens to resolve the relative path from src/styles and because npm hoists a flat node_modules; it breaks under pnpm/yarn PnP layouts, and silently breaks if the Fontsource packages rename their internal files/ directory (the path is not part of their export map, so no resolver or type check guards it — the failure mode is fonts quietly falling back at runtime). The supported pattern is importing the package's own CSS (e.g. `import '@fontsource-variable/inter'`) or using a Vite alias into the package.
findings.suggestion: Replace the hand-written @font-face blocks with the Fontsource-provided CSS imports (which also fixes the flagged legacy format() string), or reference the files through the package export map so resolution is validated at build time.
findings.verifyNote: The premise is accurate — src/styles/fonts.css:8,16,24 do hardcode relative `../../node_modules/@fontsource-variable/.../files/*.woff2` paths that bypass module resolution and couple to npm's physical layout — but one detail is wrong (Fontsource's export map DOES expose "./files/*.woff2", so a bare-specifier url() would be resolver-validated; it's the relative path that skips it), the site builds fine today under Vite+npm, and the fix is a portability/maintainability judgment call rather than a current defect.

findings.summary: No clickjacking protection is possible with the current delivery: frame-ancestors cannot be set in a meta CSP and GitHub Pages sends no X-Frame-Options, so the site is freely framable.
findings.detail: The CSP is emitted as a <meta http-equiv> tag (GitHub Pages cannot set response headers), and the frame-ancestors directive is explicitly ignored in meta-delivered policies, so any site can iframe https://ramuroy.github.io for overlay/UI-redress tricks against visitors. Low practical risk for a portfolio, but it is an unexamined, undocumented gap in an otherwise deliberately documented security posture (docs/decisions.md D-005 discusses the CSP without mentioning this limitation).
findings.suggestion: Record the accepted risk in docs/decisions.md, or if framing protection is wanted, move hosting behind a proxy that can send frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options headers (e.g. Cloudflare Pages/Netlify in front of the same repo).
findings.verifyNote: Premise fully accurate — CSP is meta-delivered (astro.config.mjs:12-28, confirmed in dist/index.html and scripts/check-build.mjs:30), frame-ancestors is spec-ignored in meta CSP, GitHub Pages sends no framing headers, and docs/decisions.md D-005 never mentions it — but for a static portfolio with no authenticated UI, treating this undocumented accepted risk as an issue is a judgment call.

findings.summary: Two untracked audit scratch files (docs/audit-notes-wip.md, docs/site-audit-2026-07-16.md) are sitting inside the tracked docs/ tree and will be swept into the next commit by any `git add docs/` or `git add -A`.
findings.detail: git status --porcelain shows `?? docs/audit-notes-wip.md` and `?? docs/site-audit-2026-07-16.md` (dated 2026-07-16, i.e. produced during this audit session). They are not covered by .gitignore, live next to the curated documentation set governed by docs/README.md's maintenance rules, and would publish internal audit notes to the public repository if committed accidentally.
findings.suggestion: Delete them or move them outside the repository (they are working notes, not project docs); if audit notes must live in-repo temporarily, add a docs/*-wip.md / scratch pattern to .gitignore.
findings.verifyNote: git status --porcelain shows both `?? docs/audit-notes-wip.md` and `?? docs/site-audit-2026-07-16.md` as untracked, .gitignore (build/deps/editor patterns only, ending at `.design/`) does not cover them, and their contents are internal audit scratch notes (session-recovery paths, workflow IDs, WIP findings) that a `git add docs/` or `git add -A` would stage into the public repo exactly as claimed.

findings.summary: The downloadable CV is an untagged PDF with empty Title/Author metadata, so it is inaccessible to screen readers and shows a blank title in browser tabs.
findings.detail: pdfinfo reports Tagged: no, Title: (empty), Author: (empty) (LaTeX/pdfTeX output). Untagged PDFs have no reading-order or structure information for assistive technology, and the missing document title means the primary artifact a recruiter downloads is the least accessible thing the site serves — on a site that otherwise treats accessibility as a requirement. No auditor examined the PDF at all.
findings.suggestion: Regenerate the resume with tagging and metadata (e.g. LaTeX: \usepackage[tagged]{accessibility} or lualatex-based tagging, plus \hypersetup{pdftitle={Ramu Roy — Embedded Systems Engineer}, pdfauthor={Ramu Roy}}).
findings.verifyNote: pdfinfo on public/Ramu_Roy_Resume.pdf confirms Tagged: no and empty Title/Author (pdfTeX output), so the untagged/metadata-less PDF claim is factually accurate; only nuance is browsers show the filename, not a blank tab title.

findings.summary: The copyright year "© 2026" is hardcoded in the footer and will silently go stale.
findings.detail: Footer.astro renders the literal string `© 2026 {profile.name}`. The project's own architecture doc (docs/architecture.md, 'Content model and derived values') mandates deriving values rather than duplicating literals, yet the year is a hardcoded literal that nobody flagged. In January 2027 the site advertises a stale year until someone remembers to edit it.
findings.suggestion: Compute it at build time in the frontmatter: `const year = new Date().getFullYear();` and render `© {year}` (the site rebuilds on every deploy, which is sufficient for a portfolio).
findings.verifyNote: Footer.astro:17 does render the hardcoded literal `© 2026 {profile.name}` with no derived year anywhere in the frontmatter or data files, so the copyright will silently go stale.

findings.summary: The hero lead's authored spaces are silently discarded: arrow segments render only the label, dropping seg.t (" "), so the text content is "hardware→firmware→custom Linux" with no spaces.
findings.detail: In site.ts the lead data models each arrow as { t: " ", arrow: true, label: "→" }, but the template branch `seg.arrow ? {seg.label} : ...` never outputs seg.t. dist/index.html confirms `hardware→firmware`. The visual gap is faked by padding-inline on .arrow, but selected/copied text and the accessibility-tree string have no word boundaries between the stack layers, and any future consumer of the data's spaces gets different output than authored.
findings.suggestion: Render the space too: `{seg.t !== " " ? seg.t : ""}{seg.label} ` or simply include literal spaces around the arrow span in the template.
findings.verifyNote: Verified: src/data/site.ts:64/66/68 model arrows as { t: " ", arrow: true, label: "→" }, Hero.astro:19-20 renders only {seg.label} and drops seg.t, dist/index.html contains the space-less hardware→firmware, and the visual gap comes solely from padding-inline: 0.15em at src/styles/global.css:261 — so copied/accessible text really has no word boundaries between layers.

findings.summary: class={cond ? "is-active" : ""} emits valueless `<dd class>` attributes throughout the built HTML instead of omitting the attribute.
findings.detail: Hero.astro:52, About.astro:38, and Projects.astro:45 use the ternary-empty-string pattern, so dist/index.html contains a dozen `<dd class>` fragments (verified). It is parseable HTML but is serializer noise, defeats attribute-based tooling/diffing, and diverges from the class:list idiom used everywhere else in the codebase.
findings.suggestion: Use `class:list={[{ "is-active": s.active }]}` or `class={s.active ? "is-active" : undefined}` so Astro omits the attribute entirely.
findings.verifyNote: Verified: the ternary-empty-string pattern is present at Hero.astro:52, About.astro:38, and Projects.astro:45, and dist/index.html contains 15 valueless `<dd class>` attributes, confirming Astro emits the bare attribute instead of omitting it (polish-level issue).

findings.summary: Decorative glyphs are inconsistently exposed to screen readers: "GitHub ↗" (nav), "back to top ↑" (footer), and "skip intro ▸" (boot) announce raw arrow characters while identical glyphs elsewhere are aria-hidden.
findings.detail: Projects/Certifications/CTA arrows are wrapped in <span aria-hidden="true">, but the nav GitHub link (Nav.astro:15), footer back-to-top link (Footer.astro:22), and boot skip button (BootIntro.astro:5) embed ↗/↑/▸ directly in the accessible name, producing announcements like "GitHub north east arrow, link". Similarly the "//" prefixes in eyebrows, the contact/footer availability LEDs ("// available for embedded roles"), and the colophon "rr@embedded:~$" are all in accessible text and read aloud as slash-slash/tilde noise.
findings.suggestion: Wrap all decorative glyphs and "//"-style prefixes in aria-hidden spans (matching the pattern already used in Projects/Hero), keeping clean accessible names such as "GitHub", "Back to top", "Skip intro".
findings.verifyNote: Verified: Nav.astro:15 (`GitHub ↗`), Footer.astro:22 (`back to top ↑`), and BootIntro.astro:5 (`skip intro ▸`) embed glyphs in accessible names, while Certifications.astro:25, Contact.astro:47, and Projects.astro:61/78 wrap the same glyphs in aria-hidden spans — the inconsistency and the `//`/colophon noise (Footer.astro:10,14) are real.

findings.summary: Each grid project card is a single <a> wrapping the entire card, giving screen-reader users link names 25+ words long (title + date + description + badges + category + stars).
findings.detail: The gcard anchor wraps title, date, full description paragraph, all tech badges, category, and star count, so the accessible name of the link (computed from contents) is e.g. "Transformerless Power Supply Aug 2024 A 220V AC → 5V DC transformerless power supply designed in KiCad. KiCad PCB Hardware/PCB ★ 3". Links lists and Tab navigation become unwieldy, and every element inside loses independent selectability.
findings.suggestion: Use the standard card pattern: make only the title the link and expand its hit area with a ::after pseudo-element overlay (position:absolute; inset:0) on the card, or add aria-label={g.title} to the anchor.
findings.verifyNote: Projects.astro:106 wraps title, date, description, badges, category, and stars in a single anchor with no aria-label, so the link's accessible name is the entire card content as claimed.

findings.summary: Both certificate links point at Google Drive share URLs — an external dependency that can silently break, may demand a Google login, and undercuts the site's self-contained/no-trackers posture.
findings.detail: certifications[].url are drive.google.com/file/d/... links with usp=sharing/usp=drive_link tokens. Drive links rot when the owner's sharing settings, account, or file organization changes, load an interstitial viewer requiring Google cookies, and are the only off-github external resources on the page. Nobody verified they are world-readable. The SEO auditor flagged only the duplicate anchor text, not the hosting choice.
findings.suggestion: Export the two NPTEL certificates as PDFs into public/certs/ and link them same-origin (they are already public documents), keeping the Drive links as nothing more than a fallback.
findings.verifyNote: src/data/site.ts:299-300 do link both NPTEL certifications to drive.google.com share URLs as claimed, but link-rot/self-hosting concerns are a polish-level judgment call, not a verifiable defect.

findings.summary: The @ts-expect-error on Astro.csp.insertDirective will hard-fail `npm run check` (and thus every deploy) the moment Astro adds 'style-src-attr' to its directive union type.
findings.detail: @ts-expect-error errors when the following line stops producing a type error. Astro upgrading its CspDirective type to include style-src-attr (the comment says the union does not include it "yet") turns this line into an unused suppression, astro check reports it as an error, and the verify gate blocks all deployments after a routine `^7` minor upgrade — a time-bomb in the release path.
findings.suggestion: Replace @ts-expect-error with a type assertion that survives both states, e.g. `Astro.csp?.insertDirective("style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'" as Parameters<NonNullable<typeof Astro.csp>["insertDirective"]>[0])` or a targeted `as never`/`as any` cast with the explanatory comment kept.
findings.verifyNote: src/layouts/Layout.astro:10 has the @ts-expect-error as described, astro check runs in npm run verify which gates the GitHub Pages deploy workflow, so an Astro type-union widening would turn the suppression into a TS2578 error and block deploys after a lockfile bump.

findings.summary: prefers-reduced-motion is sampled once at script evaluation and never observed, so toggling the OS setting mid-session leaves all animations running (or suppressed) until a full reload.
findings.detail: Layout.astro:86, Hero.astro:72, and BootIntro.astro:31 each read matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches into a const with no change listener. A user who enables reduce-motion while the page is open keeps the infinite canvas loop, scramble hover effect, count-ups and cursor glow (the CSS side updates live, the JS side does not) — an inconsistent half-reduced state on a site that names reduced-motion a hard requirement.
findings.suggestion: Keep a live MediaQueryList and register a change listener that stops the rAF loop, cancels scramble timers, and skips future JS-driven animation when matches becomes true.
findings.verifyNote: All three cited locations read matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches once into a const with no change listener (the only MQL change listener is the 721px nav one at Layout.astro:249), while global.css handles the preference via live @media blocks — so a mid-session toggle really does leave JS-driven animations (Hero canvas loop, scramble, count-ups, cursor glow) in their page-load state.

findings.summary: Repeated copies of the same value are never announced: the aria-live region is set to an identical string, which screen readers do not re-announce, and the region is never cleared.
findings.detail: copyStatus.textContent = `${prevLabel} copied to clipboard.` writes the same string on every successful copy of the same button. aria-live regions only announce on DOM mutation producing changed content; setting textContent to its current value is a no-op in most AT (NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver), so the second press of "Copy email" gives a sighted user the "copied ✓" flash but a blind user silence. The stale message also lingers in the accessibility tree indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Clear the region first and write on the next frame (copyStatus.textContent = ""; requestAnimationFrame(() => copyStatus.textContent = msg)), or append a zero-width variation/timestamped node, and clear the region after a few seconds.
findings.verifyNote: Premise verified: Layout.astro:210 rewrites the identical string into the aria-live="polite" region (Contact.astro:44) and no code ever clears it, but whether AT actually skips re-announcing identical replaced text varies by screen reader/browser, so the silent-second-press outcome is likely rather than certain.

findings.summary: Three OFL-licensed font files are redistributed in dist/_astro without any license/attribution notice anywhere in the repo or site.
findings.detail: Inter, JetBrains Mono, and Space Grotesk are SIL OFL 1.1; the built site serves the .woff2 binaries from its own origin. The OFL permits web-font use but expects the license and copyright notices to accompany redistributed font software where practical; the repo has no LICENSE file at all (flagged separately) and no font attribution in README, docs, or a colophon. Trivial to fix and eliminates any ambiguity for a public repo that redistributes the binaries.
findings.suggestion: Add a NOTICE/CREDITS section to README (or a licenses paragraph in the footer/colophon) naming the three typefaces, their copyright holders, and the SIL OFL 1.1, and include the OFL text alongside the repo's own LICENSE when it is added.
findings.verifyNote: Premise checks out — src/styles/fonts.css self-hosts Inter, JetBrains Mono, and Space Grotesk (OFL 1.1) from Fontsource, and there is no LICENSE file or OFL/attribution notice anywhere in the repo, README, or site — but dist/ is not git-tracked (only the deployed site serves the binaries), woff2 files carry embedded copyright metadata, and the OFL FAQ explicitly permits @font-face web serving, so whether an external notice is required is a best-practice judgment call rather than a factual defect.

findings.summary: display:contents on the <dl> inside .pcard__params risks stripping the definition-list semantics from the accessibility tree in some browsers.
findings.detail: `.pcard__params.cols .spec { display: contents; }` is applied to a <dl> so its .spec__row divs become grid items of the parent. display:contents has a long history of removing elements' implicit ARIA roles (list/table semantics) from the accessibility tree — fixed at different times across Chromium/WebKit/Gecko and still buggy for some roles in older-but-supported Safari versions — so the key/value pairs may be exposed as flat text without list structure.
findings.suggestion: Make the grid the <dl> itself (apply the two-column grid directly to .spec inside .cols and drop the wrapper), avoiding display:contents on a semantically meaningful element.
findings.verifyNote: Premise verified — global.css:308 applies display:contents to the <dl class="spec"> in Projects.astro:41 with no ARIA role backstop or cascade override — but the role-stripping bug is fixed in current browsers, so the residual impact (older Safari, inconsistent SR handling of <dl> anyway) is a polish-level judgment call.

findings.summary: Printing with JS enabled before scrolling the page yields invisible trace dividers (and same-pattern gaps): the print stylesheet resets .reveal/.fade opacity but not the JS-gated stroke-dashoffset/scaleX/width states.
findings.detail: `.js.reveal-ready .trace-div path { stroke-dashoffset: var(--len) }` hides the divider stroke until an in-view class arrives from IntersectionObserver. The @media print block (lines 500-508) forces opacity/transform for .reveal/.fade only; a user who opens the page and immediately prints (Ctrl+P without scrolling) gets .trace-div paths still at full dashoffset — and unlike the background-based gauge fills already flagged, SVG strokes DO print, so this is a distinct mechanism. .section-head .rule scaleX(0) and .gauge__fill width:0 have the same unreset JS-gated state.
findings.suggestion: In @media print add: `.js.reveal-ready .trace-div path { stroke-dashoffset: 0 !important } .js.reveal-ready .trace-div circle { opacity: 1 !important } .js.reveal-ready .section-head .rule { transform: none !important } .js.reveal-ready .gauge__fill { width: var(--w) !important }`.
findings.verifyNote: Verified: global.css:433/437 (trace paths/circles), :120 (.rule scaleX(0)), :395 (.gauge__fill width:0) are all JS-gated hidden states not reset in the @media print block (lines 500-508, which only fixes .reveal/.fade), the resets at lines 517-521 live in the prefers-reduced-motion block not print, and Layout.astro has no beforeprint handler — so printing before elements scroll into view yields invisible dividers/rules/gauge fills.

refuted.summary: Global :focus-visible rule forces border-radius: var(--radius-sm) on every focusable element, visibly morphing elements that have a different radius.
refuted.refutation: The rule uses :where(), giving it specificity (0,1,0); .copy-btn (global.css:411) ties and comes later in source order so its radius-xs wins while focused, and .btn-primary:hover (0,2,0) outranks the focus rule so the glow-ring is not replaced — the claimed morphing cannot occur.

tiers.name: Tier 1 — Do first: recruiter-critical content (small diffs, highest screening impact)

items.title: Measured outcomes rendered as datasheet tables on every flagship
items.why: Merges recruiter-lens 'measurable outcomes' with brand-designer 'Electrical Characteristics table' — they are the same fix. No project on the page has a single quantified result (src/data/site.ts:133-139, 158-164, 183-189 list platforms, not numbers), which is the biggest gap between this site and a top-tier embedded portfolio; meanwhile the eyebrows already promise a datasheet ('// 04 — specifications') that the soft dotted-leader params never deliver. Real numbers presented as TABLE 1-1 fixes the content gap and lands the strongest brand move in one change.
items.sketch: Extend Flagship in src/data/site.ts:101-115 with metrics: {k, v, note?}[] and roleLine: string. Collect real numbers: anti-collision — UWB ranging rate (Hz), zone-decision→relay-trip latency (ms), node/crane count, months in production; eOS — WIC image size (MB), cold-boot time (s), A/B swap+verify time, recipe count; voice — wake-word FAR/hr and FRR %, Whisper real-time factor on Pi 5, barge-in latency (ms). In src/components/Projects.astro:40-49 render params+metrics as <table class="ds-table"> with <caption>TABLE 1-1 · OPERATING CHARACTERISTICS</caption>: mono uppercase th (PARAMETER / CONDITIONS / VALUE), 1px var(--border) row rules, font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, right-aligned values in var(--text); keep .spec dotted leaders for hero/about/contact. Add roleLine ('Sole firmware engineer, 6-month engagement') under the tagline. Wrap the table in an overflow-x:auto div. Pure HTML/CSS, zero JS, no CSP impact.

items.title: Restructure for the 30-second screen: reorder sections, kill the thrice-told resume, proof-first ticker
items.why: Merges recruiter-lens 'distinct job per section' + 'reorder for the 30-second screen' — both are one IA pass over site.ts and index.astro. About paragraphs 2-3 (site.ts:88-89) restate the Radiogeet/Elipse experience entries and flagship cards almost clause-for-clause ('BitBake PR bumps, AUTOREV pinning, IPK packaging' appears three times on one page), a screener hits three dense paragraphs before any project card (index.astro:13-20), the ticker leads with 'cgpa 8.3' (site.ts:74), and CGPA appears four times. Every scroll-stop must deliver new information, strongest fact first.
items.sketch: In src/pages/index.astro move <Projects /> above <About />; renumber the data-driven sections map (site.ts:315-322) to match. Cut about.paragraphs (site.ts:86-90) to one narrative paragraph (the seams-between-layers framing) plus one sentence on the role he wants. Trim experience[].highlights (site.ts:244-251, 262-267) to ≤3 bullets per role, dropping bullets duplicated in flagship cards; end trimmed roles with 'Full detail: FIG. 01/02' as #projects anchor links (work without JS). Reorder ticker to lead with 'deployed @ Tata Steel BlueScope', 'custom Yocto distro in active dev', '100% on-device voice'; delete 'cgpa 8.3' and the repo count from it. Remove CGPA from about.glance (site.ts:94), keeping it only in hero keySpecs and Education.

items.title: Scope-honest verbs: the site must never outbid the resume
items.why: Recruiter-lens, kept intact. The Elipse role started May 2026 (site.ts:239) — roughly ten weeks before today — yet the first highlight claims 'Architected a Yocto/OpenEmbedded distro' (site.ts:245) while the linked PDF says 'Contributing to'. Screeners open both, and a site that out-claims the resume is one of the fastest credibility killers in embedded hiring; it also taints the genuinely strong Tata Steel claims. Subsystem ownership is credible at this tenure and more informative than whole-system authorship.
items.sketch: Edit site.ts:242-250: replace 'Architected a Yocto/OpenEmbedded distro…' with ownership framing — 'Own the OTA/build pipeline, the Rust sensor-fusion framework, and the voice subsystem within eOS' — keeping the concrete detail (recipes, BitBake PR bumps, AUTOREV, IPK). Apply the same pass to flagship 1 highlights (site.ts:127-130): keep 'Authored recipes' and 'Built the voice subsystem'; downgrade any whole-distro authorship verb where the resume says contribute. Write the rule into docs/decisions.md: the site may add detail and evidence over the PDF, never bigger verbs.

items.title: Contact conversion pack: persistent nav CTA, EMAIL ME, prefilled mailto, logistics answered
items.why: Merges recruiter-lens 'cut contact friction' + 'logistics block' — both are the same conversion fix at the same touchpoints. The two actions a convinced recruiter takes (email, CV) live only at the extreme bottom of a long page — the sticky nav (src/components/Nav.astro:10-17) has five section links plus GitHub but no email or CV; the CTA is developer-speak 'OPEN MAILTO' (Contact.astro:47); and 'AVAILABLE' (site.ts:20-21) next to 'May 2026 – Present' employment is a contradiction with no notice-period, relocation, or start-date answer — ambiguity screeners resolve by skipping the candidate.
items.sketch: Add a small <a class="btn btn-primary" href=mailto:…> plus the CV link as the final items in Nav.astro's list (visible on desktop, inside the existing mobile menu). Change every mailto to mailto:royramu694429@gmail.com?subject=Embedded%20role%20%E2%80%94%20via%20portfolio. Rename 'OPEN MAILTO' → 'EMAIL ME' in Contact.astro:47. Add a logistics object to site.ts (availableFrom, noticePeriod, workMode, relocation) rendered as three extra spec rows in the Contact dl (Contact.astro:16-43); reword the status pill to a fact — 'open to embedded roles · 30-day notice'. Optional: a public/rr.vcf vCard link beside the copy buttons. Pure HTML, zero JS, zero CSP impact.

items.title: Credibility sweep: hide tiny star counts, fix inflated titles, real NPTEL verify links, demote the gauges
items.why: Merges recruiter-lens 'red-flags' + 'cert links' — one pass removing everything that fails a senior engineer's click-through. The Tata Steel flagship advertises '★ 1' (site.ts:166), the grid sorts by stars so a hobby PSU outranks the RTOS work (Projects.astro:7), 'Object Detection over SPI' (site.ts:213) is an IR proximity sensor — a computer-vision claim a click disproves — and both cert links are consumer Google Drive scans (site.ts:299-300) while the animated 85%/88% gauges (Certifications.astro:17-22) give two online courses more ceremony than the production deployment gets.
items.sketch: In Projects.astro drop the star field from cards (or gate stars >= 10) and sort the featured grid by a curated order field or by category instead of stars. Rename site.ts:213 to 'IR Presence Detection over SPI (ESP32 ↔ Arduino)'; unfeature 'Fire Detection System' (site.ts:214). Replace both cert urls with the official NPTEL verification URLs printed on the certificates and relabel 'view certificate' → 'verify ↗' (Certifications.astro:24). Drop the gauge bars, render each cert as one spec row (title · NPTEL 2025 · 85% · verify) inside the education spec-card (Experience.astro:34-46), retire standalone section 05, and renumber the sections map (site.ts:315-322) — nav (site.ts:42-48) has no certifications link, so nothing else breaks.

items.title: Proof stats under the hero — then dress them as a scope capture
items.why: Merges recruiter-lens 'proof stats' (the must) with brand-designer 'oscilloscope stats band' (the optional dressing). '19 GitHub repos · 18 projects · 12 protocols · 5 languages' (Stats.astro:5-10) spends the most valuable slot on the page on volume counts screeners read as junior padding, while the rare facts — production safety system, custom distro, fully on-device voice — sit below the fold. The scope-measurement framing only becomes honest once the numbers are measurements of real outcomes, so data ships first.
items.sketch: Phase 1 (S, ship now): rework the stats array in Stats.astro keeping the D-009 derived pattern — '1 safety system live in production', 'N months @ Tata Steel BlueScope' (derive N from a deploymentDate constant in site.ts so it never goes stale), '3 stack layers owned — PCB / firmware / distro', '0 cloud deps in the voice pipeline'; keep count-up + no-JS fallback (Layout.astro:303-345) untouched; retire githubRepoCount (site.ts:16) from the strip. Phase 2 (M, optional): .stats--scope wrapper — graticule via two repeating-linear-gradients at calc(100%/10)/calc(100%/8) in var(--grid-line), per-stat CH{n} mono chip with per-channel nth-child colors, corner "TRIG'D · AUTO" in var(--success). All static CSS.

tiers.name: Tier 2 — Strong upgrades: verifiable evidence and a sharpened identity

items.title: Publish verifiable public artifacts for the two closed-source flagships
items.why: Recruiter-lens, kept intact. Two of three flagships end in 'no public repo' (site.ts:140, 190) — the strongest work is unverifiable while the verifiable repos are Arduino starters, exactly backwards for a screener. A standalone wake-word repo (training → ONNX → tract inference with a benchmark README) touches no Elipse IP, and an eOS architecture write-up costs nothing proprietary. Off-site work, but it converts the hiring case from claimed to checkable — and gives Tier 1's metrics table its receipts.
items.sketch: (1) Public wake-word repo: training script, ONNX export, a Rust crate running tract inference, README benchmark table (model size, FAR/hr, FRR, inference ms on Pi 5); set it as flagship 3's repo field replacing noRepoNote (site.ts:190). (2) 'eos-architecture-notes' repo or long-form README: block diagram, recipe-layer layout, A/B OTA flow, D-Bus interface sketches (interface names are already public on this site, site.ts:128); link from flagship 1 as 'REF → architecture write-up' (site.ts:140). Pin both on the GitHub profile so its above-the-fold matches the site's flagships. Clear the write-up with Elipse first.

items.title: Ship visual evidence: bench photos, KiCad renders, and a voice-pipeline block diagram
items.why: Merges recruiter-lens 'visual evidence' (the umbrella) with tech-showcase 'voice-pipeline signal-flow diagram' (the strongest single artifact within it). The site contains zero images of actual work for a candidate whose pitch is 'I build hardware' — recruiters treat rig photos as the strongest authenticity signal. The pipeline diagram with data-rate and latency annotations is the lingua franca of embedded design reviews, and it reuses the existing circuit-pulse animation system (global.css:448) so reduced-motion (global.css:522) and no-JS come free.
items.sketch: Add media: {src, alt, caption}[] to Flagship/GridProject types in site.ts; render as

items.title: Protocol-decode trace dividers (correct I2C / UART / SPI frames, computed at build time)
items.why: Merges tech-showcase 'protocol-decode dividers' (primary — the waveforms carry information and are provably correct by construction) with brand-designer 'PCB grammar dividers' (absorbed: the variant-prop mechanism and annular-ring pads; the pure-scenery refdes/serpentine dies). The current divider is one generic wavy path (TraceDivider.astro:5). A correctly decoded transaction — start bit, ACK on the 9th clock, LSB-first order — is the kind of detail senior engineers actively check, and the site already generates deterministic SVG in frontmatter (Circuit.astro:1-47), so this is the same technique pointed at real content.
items.sketch: Extend TraceDivider.astro with Props { protocol: 'i2c'|'spi'|'uart', byte?: number, addr?: number }. Pure frontmatter function converts a byte to {t, level} edges per channel (UART: idle-high, start low, 8 data bits LSB-first, stop; I2C: SDA transitions only while SCL low, ACK on clock 9); emit H/V step <path>s on 2-3 rails 8px apart (bump viewBox height to ~48) plus <text> decode labels ('S', '0x3C', 'W', 'ACK', 'P') in var(--font-mono) at var(--fs-micro), fill var(--silkscreen). Set --len to the computed path length so the existing draw-on-scroll (global.css:432-439) and reduced-motion override (global.css:520) work unchanged. Different protocol/byte per call site (About.astro:45, Projects.astro:72, Footer.astro:7). Add an SVG <title> with the decode; keep aria-hidden. Zero JS.

items.title: Three-voice palette: copper board, cyan signal, phosphor terminal
items.why: Merges brand-designer 'two-metal color system' + 'phosphor terminal voice' into one token-surgery pass. Everything decorative and everything interactive is the same cyan (#00E5FF via --accent, with --trace a dark cyan #16323D), which flattens hierarchy and reads generic-techy. Copper for static PCB scenery, cyan strictly for live signal, phosphor green for the terminal moments (boot overlay, footer prompt): each color means something — the difference between an art-directed site and a themed one. Decorative-only usage, so no text-contrast obligations; zero JS; no motion implications.
items.sketch: tokens.css: add --copper:#B87333; --copper-dim:#6E4A26; --pad-gold:#D4A24E; --phosphor:#3AFB77; --phosphor-dim:#1E7A42; --phosphor-glow:rgba(58,251,119,0.25). Repoint consumers to copper: .circuit__base/.circuit__via/.circuit__pad (global.css:445-447), .trace-div path (432), .tl-item::before (345), .ticked::before/::after (180-181). Keep cyan for .circuit__pulse, .signal-rail__fill, all hover/focus/link states, active spec values. Phosphor: .boot__line .ok (global.css:243) and the boot .caret; .footer__colophon .accent + footer caret (global.css:421-422); optional static scanline gradient on .boot only. Leave --success green for the LED/deployed pills. Check the result against the OG image and favicon for palette drift.

items.title: Partition-map exhibits: RAUC A/B and ESP32 OTA layouts as datasheet bars
items.why: Tech-showcase, kept intact — the 'register-map explorer' idea landed where it is honest. Both flagship stories are fundamentally about memory layout (A/B RAUC on a WIC image; ESP-IDF OTA partitions) told only in prose today. ESP-IDF partition tables and RAUC slot layouts are public conventions, so nothing proprietary or invented; it is exactly the diagram engineers draw on whiteboards, and it is pure HTML/CSS so the no-JS and reduced-motion stories are trivially perfect.
items.sketch: New src/components/PartitionMap.astro taking { segments: {name, offset, size, note, active?}[] }, data added per Flagship in site.ts. Flex row of .pmap__seg with flex-grow: max(1, log2(sizeKB)) (linear scale makes nvs invisible); borders var(--border); the booted slot gets a var(--accent) top border + 'booted / marked good' pill. Below the bar, a .spec dl reusing the dotted-leader rows (global.css:161) listing 0x-prefixed offset / size / purpose in tabular-nums mono; per-segment :hover/:focus-within popovers on hover-capable wide screens (segments tabindex=0 with aria-describedby); always show the dl under @media (hover: none). Mount in .pcard__params of FIG. 01 (SD image: boot FAT32 → rootfs A → rootfs B → data) and FIG. 02 (nvs @0x9000, otadata, ota_0, ota_1, spiffs). Skip the OTA-write shimmer flourish.

items.title: Boot log that reads like a real bring-up
items.why: Merges tech-showcase 'real eOS boot log' (primary: it is a data change) with the salvageable parts of motion-director's 'BootIntro v2' (timing budget, grouped beats); the per-character typing and hero-handoff morph are killed separately. The current three lines (site.ts:51-55) read as a themed splash; dmesg-style timestamps, 'rauc: booted slot A, marking good', 'eos-voice: KWS model loaded (tract)' turn the first 1.5 seconds into resume content a technical screener absorbs involuntarily. All the D-007 accessibility hardening stays untouched.
items.sketch: Extend bootLines in site.ts to ~8-10 typed entries { ts, text, status?: 'ok', group } using only facts already published on this page (verify employer comfort per eOS). Generalize BootIntro.astro's split logic (line 8) to the typed shape — no set:html, per D-008. Render timestamps '[    0.0421]' in var(--muted), message var(--text-secondary), '[ ok ]' in accent (phosphor once the palette item lands). Drive animation-delay from group, not index, so 10 lines land in 3 beats within ~1300ms; bump the auto-dismiss timer (BootIntro.astro:74) to ~1700ms; skip button, Escape, and reduced-motion bypass (BootIntro.astro:39-42) unchanged. Export the array for any future dmesg/terminal reuse.

items.title: Motion discipline: infinite loops mean status; reduced motion keeps feedback
items.why: Merges motion-director 'retire the infinite shimmer' + 'design the reduced-motion mode' — two halves of one policy: motion must mean something. Six simultaneous infinite loops (title shimmer 7s on every heading global.css:483, LED breathe :189, rail-node ping :201, pill pulse-dots :143, circuit pulses :448, caret blink :245, plus nudge :273) is the biggest 'template' tell on the site and keeps the compositor busy for the page's life. Meanwhile the blanket reduced-motion kill (global.css:513-527) also destroys harmless opacity/color feedback like the copy-button confirmation — WCAG targets vestibular triggers, not crossfades; a curated policy is the craft an accessibility-literate reviewer looks for.
items.sketch: Shimmer becomes event-driven: '.section-head.in-view .section-head__title { animation: shimmer 1.8s var(--ease-std) .3s 1 both }' plus a :hover replay; arrange gradient stops so the resting state is pure var(--text) (no-JS titles already fall back correctly). Drop the .signal-rail__node ping (global.css:201) to a static glow; slow pill pulse-dot to 3.5s. Keep LED breathe + circuit pulses (status identity). Replace the universal RM rule (global.css:514) with a scoped policy: keep transitions of color/background-color/border-color/opacity/box-shadow at a new --t-rm:150ms; enumerate kills for all transform transitions, every loop above, the circuit parallax, and scroll-linked movement. Add a matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') change listener in Layout.astro so mid-session OS toggles stop the canvas and cursor effects. Record 'motion = movement; feedback = opacity/color; infinite = status only' in docs/decisions.md.

items.title: Fix the dead scroll-spy styling, then nav underline polish
items.why: Motion-director's micro-polish item, promoted because it contains a confirmed live defect: CSS styles .nav__link[aria-current="true"] (global.css:217-218) but the scroll-spy sets aria-current="location" (Layout.astro:135) — the active-section indicator has never rendered on the deployed site. Verify the bottom-of-page contact override (Layout.astro:152-158) now visibly highlights Contact.

items.title: IC topmark under the hero name
items.why: Brand-designer, kept intact minus the CGPA content (Tier 1 de-emphasizes the grade). Every embedded engineer has read a thousand chip topmarks; presenting the candidate as one — mono, letter-spaced, silkscreen gray, pin-1 dot before the H1 — is the cheapest signature moment proposed, gives the loose ticker line a diegetic home, and works with zero JS. This is wit in the site's own material language, not a bolted-on joke.

Pin-1 dot: .hero h1::before { content:''; display:inline-block; width:.35em; height:.35em; border-radius:50%; background:var(--accent); margin-right:.3em; vertical-align:super; box-shadow:0 0 8px var(--glow) }. tiers.name: Tier 3 — Stretch: interactive artifacts, platform craft, and polish

items.title: PCB layer viewer from his real KiCad boards (CSS-only toggles)

items.title: Replace the constellation canvas with an oscilloscope scene (plus static SVG fallback)
items.why: Merges tech-showcase 'oscilloscope hero' (primary: transmitting real ticker strings as correctly framed UART bytes is provable domain fluency and pairs with the protocol dividers) with motion-director's 'hero canvas v2' (absorbed: the server-rendered static trace layer so no-JS/reduced-motion heroes are not visually flat, and the visibilitychange pause). The particles-and-lines canvas (Hero.astro:74-153) is the last template element on an otherwise domain-specific page.
items.sketch: Rewrite the Hero.astro canvas script: precompute UART frames (LSB-first, start/stop bits) of the ticker strings as a step function; scroll right-to-left ~60px/s with phosphor persistence (redraw previous frame at globalAlpha 0.35 instead of clearRect); 10×8 graticule via 1px lines at rgba(124,140,255,0.06); fillText the decoded ASCII char after each frame clears the trigger point; pointer becomes Δt/ΔV measurement cursors ('Δt=347µs · 1/Δt=2.88kHz') replacing mouse-attraction. Keep DPR≤2, the IO pause (Hero.astro:143-150), and the reduce guard (Hero.astro:77) verbatim; add a document.visibilitychange pause. items.title: Print as a datasheet (and skip the light theme)
items.why: Merges brand-designer 'datasheet paper print stylesheet' + tech-showcase 'print-to-datasheet mode' — the same idea from two lenses, including the same correct verdict on a light theme (40+ tokens, canvas colors hardcoded at Hero.astro:117-130, brand dilution — not worth it). '// 06 — contact & ordering info' (site.ts:321) pre-installs the punchline; Ctrl+P yielding a component datasheet is a memorable, useful leave-behind at zero runtime cost. Keep it 95% straight documentation, one joke maximum.
items.sketch: Expand @media print (global.css:500-508): re-declare core tokens inside the block (:root { --bg:#fff; --text:#111; --accent:#000; --border:#999; … }) so component CSS follows without per-selector overrides; @page { margin: 18mm }; fixed running header 'RR-2026 — RAMU ROY — REV 2026-A' in 8pt mono; square corners and no shadows on .pcard/.spec-card. Force engineering detail to print: .pcard__details > ul { display:block !important } with summary de-chromed — verify in Chromium print preview, since details content is print-hidden today. items.title: CSS scroll-driven migration: signal rail, reveals, counters
items.why: Merges motion-director's three scroll-driven items (rail/parallax, view() reveals, @property counter) into one @supports-gated system change. Today all three run on JS observers and a scroll listener (Layout.astro:88-108, 144-168, 303-345); scroll()/view() timelines move them off the main thread and — the real prize — make them work with JS disabled, upgrading D-006 from 'fail open' to 'fully designed without JS'. The counter version also deletes the one place real markup values are zeroed by JS (Layout.astro:329-331). Devtools-literate reviewers notice compositor-driven scroll animation with no listener.
items.sketch: @supports (animation-timeline: scroll()): rail-fill keyframes (height 0%→100%) on .signal-rail__fill and a top 0%→100% keyframe on __node, animation-timeline: scroll(root); circuit-drift keyframe replacing the --scrollp translate at global.css:444. @supports (animation-timeline: view()): reveal-in on .reveal/.fade with animation-range: entry 15% entry 55% and fill-mode both (never leave text half-transparent at rest); same pattern for the .trace-div draw; inside the block neutralize the .js.reveal-ready hidden states and skip observing those elements. Counters: @property --n { syntax:'<integer>' } + counter-set rendered via ::before, per-element target in the style attr (style-src-attr already permitted, Layout.astro:11). Gate each JS system with CSS.supports so exactly one mechanism runs; keep the bottom-of-page spy fix unconditional. Route all end states through the Tier 2 reduced-motion policy. Note: the cert gauges may already be gone via the Tier 1 credibility sweep.

items.title: Footer terminal easter egg + DevTools console signature
items.why: Merges tech-showcase 'UART console' + 'console signature' (the banner is the terminal's discoverability layer). The blinking 'rr@embedded:~$' prompt (Footer.astro:14) sets up a payoff the site never delivers; a terse, accurate command set (help / whoami / ls projects / cat resume.txt / dmesg replaying the real boot log / reboot) reads as craft to the engineers who screen embedded candidates. Strictly additive: the trigger affordance is attached only by JS, so no-JS users see today's static colophon. Queued in Tier 3 because it is showmanship, not evidence — and D-012 caps how much client JS this site should carry.
items.sketch: New Terminal.astro included from Layout.astro: hidden <div role="region" aria-label="Interactive console"> with a scrollable <output> log + prompt <input>, styled from existing tokens (--code-bg, --font-mono, .ticked). Command table built from site.ts data in frontmatter (D-009); dmesg replays the Tier 2 bootLines array; 'reboot' clears the rr_boot sessionStorage key and reloads. Backtick opens when no input is focused; Escape closes and restores focus (mirror the menu handling, Layout.astro:233-238); reduced-motion prints output synchronously. Console: console.log('%c rr@embedded ', 'background:#00E5FF;color:#062A30;…', '— type portfolio.help()') + window.portfolio = { help, resume, contact } in the existing hashed script; help() mentions the backtick shortcut. ASCII source comment: verify Astro's compressHTML keeps comments, else place it before the doctype. Budget ~150 lines; if it grows, split per D-012.

items.title: Hero power-on choreography with @starting-style
items.why: Motion-director, kept intact. The hero pops in fully rendered, then the JS underline draw (Layout.astro:110-116) and name scramble fire on top — the load feels unorchestrated. A sub-1s CSS-only entrance in board-bring-up order (LED → titleblock → name → lead underlines left to right → CTAs → spec card) runs on first style pass with zero JS, so no-JS visitors get the full sequence — a genuine upgrade over the JS-only underline draw, which this deletes.

Move the per-em underline delay from JS into authored style attrs on Hero.astro's lead segments (compute the index in the site.ts lead map render, Hero.astro:17-27; keyframes already exist at global.css:267); delete the lead-drawn block from Layout.astro. Boot coordination: dispatch rr:boot-done ~150ms before removal (BootIntro.astro:63) so entrances overlap the wipe; the default no-class timing is the no-JS path. Under the Tier 2 reduced-motion policy the entrance collapses to opacity-only or instant.

items.title: Experience timeline in the instrument language
items.why: Merges brand-designer 'logic-analyzer timeline' (primary: the employment-period waveform glyph — rising edge at start, still-high with an arrow for the current role — is a genuinely elegant encoding of 'present') with motion-director's scroll-driven spine fill (absorbed as an optional @supports layer). The strongest recruiter content currently sits on the most generic visual (a line with dots, global.css:345-348). Decorative, so it queues behind everything that adds information.

After the palette item: rail → 2px var(--copper-dim), nodes → square pads with an inner hole dot (annular-ring language). Optional @supports (animation-timeline: view()): a single .timeline::after gradient fill scrubbing over the section's view-timeline with nodes lighting at animation-range: entry 45% entry 55%; static styles remain the non-supporting default; add end-state overrides in the reduced-motion policy.

items.title: Animate the engineering-detail disclosure
items.why: Motion-director, kept intact. The <details> snap (Projects.astro:51-56) is the only hard cut on the page and it sits on the highest-value content a recruiter reads. ::details-content + interpolate-size animates it natively in Chromium; Firefox/Safari keep today's instant toggle — acceptable degradation on native HTML, and the no-JS story is untouched because <details> is native.

Cascade items: .pcard__details[open] li { animation: reveal-in .35s var(--ease-out) both; animation-delay: calc(var(--i) * 40ms) } with --i authored per li in Projects.astro:54 (style-src-attr already permitted). Wrap in @supports (interpolate-size: allow-keywords). The Tier 2 reduced-motion policy makes it instant again.

items.title: Mono type craft: slashed zeros, global tabular figures, outlined numerals
items.why: Brand-designer, kept intact. Instrument output has slashed zeros and columns that never wobble; tabular-nums is currently applied piecemeal (.tnum at global.css:84 plus scattered component rules), and the giant section numerals at --faint fill read as smudges rather than drawing-frame furniture. Last-10% polish — verify the Fontsource Latin subset kept the OpenType feature tables before committing.
