Numerals: .section-head__num (global.css:109) → color: transparent; -webkit-text-stroke: 1px var(--border-bright); with @supports not (-webkit-text-stroke: 1px #000) falling back to the current --faint fill; optionally raise --fs-numeral's top clamp (tokens.css:98) toward 9rem and bleed left (-0.35em) on ≥1100px.

items.title: Elevation edge highlight + film grain to kill gradient banding
items.why: Brand-designer, kept intact. Every card shares one flat recipe (var(--surface) + 1px border) and the two large fixed radial glows (global.css:51-57) band visibly on cheap panels. A 1px inset top highlight (machined-metal edge) plus a static ~2.5% feTurbulence grain layer adds depth and hides banding for ~600 bytes; nothing moves, so reduced-motion and print need one line each. The defined-but-unused --elevated tokens (tokens.css:10-11) finally earn their keep on hover states.
items.sketch: tokens.css: add --edge-highlight: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(230,237,243,0.045) in the shadow block; append it to the box-shadows of .spec-card, .pcard, .gcard, .cert, .contact__panel. Grain: a data-URI SVG (feTurbulence type='fractalNoise' baseFrequency='0.9' numOctaves='2') as an additional background layer on body::after (global.css:51) at background-size 180px with low alpha baked into the SVG; the print block already hides body::after (global.css:503). Check the grain against the blueprint grid opacity so the layers don't moiré.

rejected.title: CAD-sheet grid exposure: drawing frame with coordinate labels (brand-designer)
rejected.reason: The viewport already stacks five fixed decorative layers — blueprint grid (body::before), circuit SVG, two radial glows (body::after), cursor glow, and the signal rail. A sixth layer of edge chrome directly contradicts the surviving motion-discipline direction (fewer ambient elements, each meaning something) and competes with the signal rail for the same edge real estate. It adds 'themed dashboard' density, not information, and its value evaporates below 1200px where most recruiters will actually view the site.

rejected.title: linear() spring easing tokens for physical micro-interactions (motion-director)
rejected.reason: Overshoot-and-settle springs are a playful consumer-app gesture that fights the precision-instrument voice every surviving item sharpens — a scope trace does not wobble past its value. The proposal also requires bumping hover transform durations to 420-500ms, making every interaction feel slower for zero recruiter value. The existing --ease-out/--ease-std tokens already read engineered; taste coherence, not cost, is the reason this dies.

rejected.title: Schematic symbols as section markers (brand-designer)
rejected.reason: Redundant once the protocol-decode dividers give each section a domain-authentic graphic that actually carries information — six more decorative SVGs in headers that already stack a giant numeral, eyebrow, drawn rule, and shimmer would dilute the iconography rather than deepen it. Hidden under 720px per its own sketch, it would also be invisible to a large share of visitors. Killed as ornament competing with a stronger surviving item for the same conceptual slot.

rejected.title: Representative MODBUS RTU / relay I-O map panel (tech-showcase)
rejected.reason: Invented 'representative' register assignments rendered in datasheet style directly beside a real production-safety deployment blurs exactly the claimed-vs-verifiable line the entire surviving direction is built on: a screener either reads the fabricated map as real (misleading) or discovers it is representative and discounts the surrounding real claims. It also drags an employer-confidentiality review into a decorative table. FIG. 02 is better served by real measured metrics (Tier 1) and the evidence layer (Tier 2); the correct-CRC flourish, while charming, cannot rescue fabricated context.

rejected.title: BootIntro v2 per-character typing and hero-handoff morph (motion-director) — choreography portion
rejected.reason: The content half (authentic dmesg lines, grouped timing, budget cap) is merged into the Tier 2 boot-log item; the remainder — steps() per-character typing, ok-status flash frames, and a getBoundingClientRect-measured morph of the last line into the hero titleblock — is over-engineering a ≤1.6s, once-per-session overlay. The handoff morph in particular adds layout measurement and a new failure mode to a component whose D-007 hardening exists precisely because its lifecycle once broke the page. The words are the credibility signal; the typing effect is not.

proposals.title: CSS scroll-driven scroll progress: signal rail and circuit parallax without JS
proposals.description: The signal rail fill/node (src/styles/global.css:195-203) and the circuit parallax (global.css:444) are driven by a JS scroll listener writing --scrollp (src/layouts/Layout.astro:144-168). Modern CSS can drive both off the document scroll timeline with zero main-thread work, and — crucially — they then work with JS disabled, strengthening the site's own progressive-enhancement story. Recruiters with devtools open will notice compositor-driven scroll animation with no scroll listener. Reduced-motion fallback: the rail is a position indicator, not decorative motion — keep the fill tracking scroll but drop the ping halo (already removed at global.css:525) and the node glow pulse; the parallax translate stays disabled (global.css:523). No-JS behavior: improves from 'rail frozen at 0%' today to fully functional in supporting browsers; non-supporting browsers keep the JS path via @supports gating.
proposals.sketch: In global.css add `@supports (animation-timeline: scroll())` block: define `@keyframes rail-fill { from { height: 0% } to { height: 100% } }` on .signal-rail__fill and a matching `top: 0% -> 100%` keyframe on .signal-rail__node, both with `animation: rail-fill auto linear both; animation-timeline: scroll(root block)`. Circuit parallax: `@keyframes circuit-drift { to { transform: translateY(-60px) } }` with the same scroll(root) timeline, removing the --scrollp dependency. In Layout.astro guard the JS updater with `if (!CSS.supports('animation-timeline: scroll()'))` so only one system runs (keep the bottom-of-page scroll-spy fix unconditionally). Inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` keep the rail animations (position feedback) but retain the existing node::after and parallax kills.

proposals.title: No-JS scroll reveals: port .reveal/.fade/.trace-div/.cert to animation-timeline: view() with fail-open @supports gate
proposals.description: All entrance reveals currently require the IntersectionObserver in Layout.astro:88-108 and are gated behind html.js.reveal-ready (global.css:99-103). CSS view-timelines can do the same choreography natively: elements animate as they enter the viewport, no observer, no .in-view class, and the reveals finally work for no-JS visitors — turning the D-006 'fail open' guarantee into 'fully designed even without JS'. It also lets reveals scrub slightly with scroll (animation-range) which reads as far more intentional than a fire-once fade. Reduced-motion fallback: inside the existing prefers-reduced-motion block, force the view-timeline animations to their end state (animation: none; opacity: 1; transform: none) exactly as the current overrides at global.css:515-521 do. No-JS behavior: reveals, trace-divider draw (global.css:431-439), and cert gauge fill (global.css:394-396) all animate in supporting browsers; in non-supporting browsers the unsupported @supports block never hides anything, so content renders fully visible — strictly fail-open per D-006.
proposals.sketch: Wrap in `@supports (animation-timeline: view())`: `.reveal { animation: reveal-in auto var(--ease-out) both; animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 10% entry 60%; animation-delay: calc(var(--i,0) * 0.001s) /* delays don't apply to scrub — instead offset animation-range per --i via a custom property: animation-range-start: calc(entry 10% + var(--i,0) * 4%) */ }` with `@keyframes reveal-in { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(16px) } }`. Same pattern for .trace-div path (stroke-dashoffset var(--len) -> 0) and .gauge__fill (width 0 -> var(--w)). Inside the @supports block also neutralize the JS-era hidden states (.js.reveal-ready .reveal { opacity: 1; transform: none; transition: none }) and skip observing those elements in Layout.astro when CSS.supports('animation-timeline: view()'). Keep the IO path as-is for Safari until view-timeline ships there. Use `animation-range: entry 15% entry 55%` so items finish revealing before mid-viewport — never leave text half-transparent at rest; alternatively use `animation-fill-mode: both` with a short range so it behaves like a trigger, not a scrub, for text blocks.

proposals.title: Hero entrance choreography with @starting-style: a designed power-on sequence
proposals.description: Today the hero has no entrance: content pops in fully rendered, then the JS underline draw (Layout.astro:110-116) and name scramble (Hero.astro:155-187) fire on top, so the load feels un-orchestrated. Design a single CSS-only power-on sequence with meaningful order that mirrors an actual board bring-up: LED eyebrow blinks on (power), titleblock flickers in (silkscreen), name resolves (MCU), lead line draws hardware->firmware->Linux->ML underlines left to right (signal path), CTAs and spec card slide in last (peripherals). Total budget under 1s so it never feels slow. Reduced-motion fallback: the global kill at global.css:514 collapses every transition to 0.01ms, so everything appears instantly — no extra work needed, but explicitly exempt opacity-only fades if adopting proposal 'Designed reduced-motion mode'. No-JS behavior: @starting-style transitions run on first style pass with zero JS, so no-JS visitors get the full choreography — a genuine upgrade over the current JS-only underline/scramble.
proposals.sketch: For each hero child add `@starting-style { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px) }` with `transition: opacity 0.5s var(--ease-out), transform 0.5s var(--ease-out); transition-delay: var(--enter, 0ms)` and stagger --enter: eyebrow 0ms, h1 80ms, lead 180ms, ctas 320ms, ticker 400ms, spec-card 320ms. Convert the underline draw to pure CSS by moving the per-em delay currently set in JS (Layout.astro:113-114) into the markup (`style={--d: ...}` per em segment in site.ts's lead map index — Hero.astro:17-27) and trigger via the same @starting-style entrance on .hero__lead (keyframes already exist: draw-underline, global.css:267). Coordinate with BootIntro: when the boot overlay is active, JS adds html.boot-hold which pauses the hero delays (`.boot-hold .hero__main > * { transition-delay: calc(var(--enter) + 1200ms) }`) — but since boot only exists with JS, the default (no class) timing is the no-JS path. Delete the now-redundant lead-drawn JS block.

proposals.title: BootIntro v2: real firmware POST with per-character typing, dmesg timing, and a handoff into the hero
proposals.description: The current boot intro (src/components/BootIntro.astro:4, lines in src/data/site.ts:51-55) is three lines that fade in as whole blocks over 1.3s — it reads as a themed splash screen, not a boot. For an embedded-systems audience the details are the credibility: dmesg-style timestamps ([ 0.000042]), a peripheral checklist that maps to the actual portfolio sections (uwb0: ranging OK, yocto: image mounted, kws: wake-word armed), monospace character-by-character typing on the command line only (steps() on inline-size in ch units), ok statuses landing with a 1-frame green flash, and the final line handing off by morphing the prompt into the hero titleblock position before the wipe. Keep the hard rules that make it respectful: 1.6s absolute cap, session-gated (BootIntro.astro:34), skip button focused, Escape works. It is already earning its cost as identity; this makes it earn it as proof of domain fluency. Reduced-motion fallback: unchanged — boot.remove() before display (BootIntro.astro:39-42), users never see it. No-JS behavior: unchanged — display:none until JS adds is-active (global.css:236), so no-JS visitors go straight to content.
proposals.sketch: Data: extend bootLines in site.ts to ~6 lines with a `type: 'cmd' | 'status' | 'ts'` field and per-line dur. Typing: `.boot__line--cmd { inline-size: 0; overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; animation: type-in calc(var(--chars) * 28ms) steps(var(--chars)) forwards }` with `@keyframes type-in { to { inline-size: var(--chars-ch) } }` where --chars/--chars-ch are authored in the style attr (already CSP-permitted via style-src-attr, Layout.astro:11). Status flash: animate a background-color keyframe on .ok from var(--success) 30% alpha to transparent over 180ms. Handoff: on dismiss, before the wipe, add .is-handoff which transforms the last line to the hero titleblock's position using a stored translate (measure once with getBoundingClientRect in the existing inline script) — or cheaper, cross-fade the wipe with the hero @starting-style choreography by dispatching rr:boot-done (already exists, BootIntro.astro:63) 150ms before removal so entrances overlap the wipe. Sum of animation-delays must stay <= 1300ms before the existing auto-dismiss timer (BootIntro.astro:74) — bump timer to 1600ms.

proposals.title: Replace JS count-up with CSS @property integer transition driven by view-timeline
proposals.description: The stats count-up (Layout.astro:303-345) zeroes real markup values with JS then rAF-animates text. The modern-CSS version — a registered @property --n of syntax '<integer>' rendered via counter() — does the same count-up entirely in CSS, triggered by animation-timeline: view(), with discrete integer interpolation handled by the engine. It deletes ~40 lines of JS, and the markup values (Stats.astro:16, Certifications.astro:21) are never zeroed at all in non-supporting browsers, tightening the fail-open guarantee of D-006. This is exactly the kind of detail that reads as 'this person knows where the platform is going'. Reduced-motion fallback: wrap the counter animation in the supports block but exclude it under prefers-reduced-motion (animation: none), leaving the server-rendered number untouched — better than today's JS branch. No-JS behavior: server-rendered numbers display as-is (identical to today's no-JS path, but now nothing can ever flash to 0).
proposals.sketch: `@property --n { syntax: '<integer>'; initial-value: 0; inherits: false }`. In `@supports (animation-timeline: view()) and (counter-set: n 1)`: `.stat__value [data-count] { counter-set: n var(--n); animation: count auto var(--ease-out) both; animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 40% entry 90%; } .stat__value [data-count]::before { content: counter(n) } .stat__value [data-count] { font-size: 0 } /* hide raw text; ::before renders at parent size */` — cleaner: put the real number in a data attribute and render exclusively via counter inside the supports block so there is no double text. Author `--n` target per element in the style attribute (`--n-target`) and keyframe `@keyframes count { from { --n: 0 } to { --n: var(--n-target) } }`. Gate the existing JS counter with CSS.supports so only one mechanism runs. Apply the same pattern to the cert gauge percentage (Certifications.astro:21) so the number and the bar fill (global.css:394) share one view-timeline and finish together.

proposals.title: Experience timeline as scroll-driven signal trace: spine fills and nodes power on as you read
proposals.description: The experience section is the strongest recruiter content but has the least motion identity: a static ::before line (global.css:345) and one pulsing node. Make the timeline behave like a PCB trace being probed: the spine fills top-to-bottom linked to the section's own view-timeline, and each .tl-item__node lights (border -> accent + glow) exactly when the fill passes it, so reading order and motion order are the same — scroll-driven storytelling with meaningful order rather than decoration. Reduced-motion fallback: spine fully filled, all nodes lit statically (the pulse-dot animation on the active node is already killed by the global reduced-motion rule at global.css:514); add explicit `animation: none` end-state overrides in the RM block. No-JS behavior: with @supports gating, supporting browsers get the full effect with no JS; non-supporting browsers show the current static spine — nothing is ever hidden.
proposals.sketch: Give .timeline `view-timeline: --tl block`. Replace the per-item ::before line with a single absolutely-positioned .timeline::before track plus a ::after fill: `@supports (animation-timeline: view())` -> `.timeline::after { background: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--accent-deep), var(--accent)); animation: rail-fill auto linear both; animation-timeline: --tl; animation-range: entry 20% exit 80%; box-shadow: 0 0 8px var(--glow-strong) }` (reuse the rail-fill keyframes from the signal-rail proposal). Nodes: each .tl-item__node gets its own `animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 45% entry 55%` firing `@keyframes node-on { to { background: var(--accent); border-color: var(--accent); box-shadow: 0 0 10px var(--glow-strong) } }` with fill-mode both — a crisp threshold, like a logic level crossing. Keep the timeline-scope property on .timeline's parent if the fill needs to live outside (timeline-scope: --tl on .container). Non-supporting browsers keep the existing static styles untouched.

proposals.title: linear() spring easing tokens for all physical micro-interactions
proposals.description: Every hover on the site (card lift global.css:299, magnetic buttons global.css:127, ref arrow global.css:321, badge glow) uses the same two cubic-beziers (tokens.css:106-107). Cubic-bezier cannot overshoot-and-settle; linear() can encode a real damped spring, and applying it selectively to the 'physical' interactions (button magnetics, card lift, details chevron rotation, copy-button success state) gives the whole site a tactile, engineered feel — springs for things that move, standard easing for things that fade. This is a one-file system upgrade that touches every micro-interaction at once. Reduced-motion fallback: unchanged — the global 0.01ms transition kill (global.css:514) makes easing irrelevant. No-JS behavior: pure CSS, all hover/focus interactions work identically without JS.
proposals.sketch: In tokens.css add: `--ease-spring: linear(0, 0.0059 0.7%, 0.0946 3.1%, 0.4926 8.9%, 0.8709 14.9%, 1.0296 19.8%, 1.0862 24.5%, 1.054 32.6%, 1.0043 45.3%, 0.9924 53.2%, 1.0011 71.4%, 1)` (a ~0.85-damping spring, ~600ms natural duration) and a snappier `--ease-spring-sm` for small elements. Progressive: `@supports (transition-timing-function: linear(0, 1))` reassigns `--ease-out: var(--ease-spring)` only for transform transitions — concretely, split the .btn transition (global.css:127) so `transform var(--t-spring, 420ms) var(--ease-spring)` while color/border keep --ease-std; same for .pcard:hover translateY and .pcard__details summary::before rotation (global.css:312). Bump those transform durations to ~420-500ms since springs need room to settle. Non-supporting browsers keep the current beziers via the custom-property fallback chain.

proposals.title: Retire the infinite title shimmer; make all ambient loops one-shot or interaction-triggered
proposals.description: The section-title shimmer runs forever on every heading (global.css:483, animation: shimmer 7s linear infinite), and it competes with the LED breathe, node ping, circuit pulses, and pill dots — five simultaneous infinite loops is the single biggest 'template' tell on this site, and it keeps the compositor busy for the page's whole life. A design-director-grade motion system reserves ambient loops for at most one or two status signifiers (the LED and the circuit pulses fit the identity) and makes everything else event-driven. Convert the shimmer to a one-shot sweep that plays when the section header enters view (the .in-view hook already exists on .section-head, Layout.astro:90), and on hover thereafter. Reduced-motion fallback: already handled — shimmer disabled and text fill restored (global.css:526); keep that rule. No-JS behavior: with the view-timeline reveal proposal the sweep can run scroll-driven without JS; otherwise no-JS titles simply show the static gradient-free text (the non-.js default), which is correct fail-open.
proposals.sketch: Change global.css:483 to animate only when triggered: `.section-head.in-view .section-head__title { animation: shimmer 1.8s var(--ease-std) 0.3s 1 both }` and `.section-head__title:hover { animation: shimmer 1.8s var(--ease-std) 1 }`. Set the resting background-position so the static state is pure var(--text) (gradient stops arranged with the accent band off-canvas). Audit remaining loops: keep .led__dot breathe (status identity) and .circuit__pulse (background signature), drop the .signal-rail__node ping (global.css:201) to a subtle static glow, and slow pill--deployed pulse-dot to 3.5s so overlapping rhythms don't strobe. Document the rule 'infinite = status only' in docs/decisions.md as a motion principle.

proposals.title: Animate the Engineering detail disclosure with ::details-content and interpolate-size
proposals.description: The flagship cards' <details> (Projects.astro:51-56) snaps open instantly — the only jarring cut on the page, and it sits on the highest-value content (the engineering highlights a recruiter actually reads). Chrome/Edge now animate details natively via ::details-content + transition-behavior: allow-discrete + interpolate-size: allow-keywords: the panel slides open with height animation and the list items can cascade in with tiny per-item delays, all CSS. Reduced-motion fallback: global transition kill makes it instant again (current behavior). No-JS behavior: <details> is native HTML — opens and closes fine with zero JS, exactly as today; the animation is a pure CSS layer on top.
proposals.sketch: `:root { interpolate-size: allow-keywords }` (safe global opt-in). `.pcard__details::details-content { block-size: 0; overflow: clip; transition: block-size 0.45s var(--ease-out), content-visibility 0.45s allow-discrete } .pcard__details[open]::details-content { block-size: auto }`. Cascade items: `.pcard__details[open] li { animation: reveal-in 0.35s var(--ease-out) both; animation-delay: calc(var(--i) * 40ms) }` — author --i per li in Projects.astro:54. Rotate the summary chevron with the spring token from the easing proposal. Wrap in @supports (interpolate-size: allow-keywords) so Firefox/Safari keep the instant toggle (acceptable degradation, still functional).

proposals.title: Hero canvas v2: constellation becomes a live schematic — 45-degree routed links, traveling packets, probe cursor
proposals.description: The current canvas (Hero.astro:74-153) is the generic particles-with-lines demo every portfolio has; for an embedded engineer it should read as a live board. Three changes make it unmistakably domain-specific: (1) route links as PCB traces — horizontal/vertical runs with 45-degree corners (matching Circuit.astro's language) instead of straight point-to-point lines; (2) send occasional bright 'packets' traveling along active links with a fading tail, like the circuit background's pulses but interactive; (3) turn the cursor into a probe: within NEAR radius the nearest node gets an oscilloscope-style ring plus a tiny monospace readout (e.g. node id + 'ranging 3.2m' style flavor strings from the UWB/voice domains) — tasteful because it is confined to the hero, fine-pointer only, and text is diegetic. Also fix the physics: O(n^2) link pass at 76 nodes is fine, but add document.visibilitychange pause alongside the existing IO pause (Hero.astro:143-150). Reduced-motion fallback: canvas never starts (existing guard Hero.astro:77); additionally render a static faint SVG of the same trace pattern behind the canvas so reduced-motion and no-JS heroes are not visually flat — static imagery is not motion. No-JS behavior: canvas is empty today; the new static SVG layer (server-rendered, same deterministic seeded generator as Circuit.astro) gives no-JS visitors a designed hero background.
proposals.sketch: Routing: for each link compute Manhattan-with-45 path (dx run, 45-degree jog, dy run — same math as Circuit.astro:23-42) and draw with ctx.lineTo segments; cache per pair while distance < LINK. Packets: maintain a small pool (max 6) of {linkRef, t} advanced by dt * speed; draw a 3px accent dot + 12px gradient tail at parametric position along the routed polyline; spawn on a Poisson timer, biased toward links near the cursor. Probe: track nearest node under NEAR; draw a 14px ring + crosshair ticks; readout via ctx.fillText in JetBrains Mono 10px, strings rotated from a const array ['uwb0 3.2m', 'i2c ack', 'mqtt pub', 'kws armed']. Static fallback layer: extract the seeded rng into a shared util, generate ~20 hero-local traces server-side into an inline SVG `<svg class="hero__traces">` at opacity 0.12 behind the canvas; hide it once the canvas starts (canvas script adds .hero--live). Perf: pause via visibilitychange + existing IO; clamp DPR at 2 (already done, Hero.astro:79).

proposals.title: Design the reduced-motion experience instead of nuking it: keep opacity fades, kill movement
proposals.description: The current reduced-motion block (global.css:513-527) sets every animation/transition to 0.01ms globally — technically compliant, but it also removes harmless, useful feedback: link underline growth, color transitions, the copy-button confirmation, focus transitions. WCAG's motion guidance targets vestibular triggers (translation, scaling, parallax), not opacity or color change. A curated reduced-motion mode — crossfades and color transitions stay at reduced durations; all transform-based motion, parallax, and loops stop — shows a level of accessibility craft that a blanket kill switch cannot, and it is the kind of detail an accessibility-literate reviewer specifically looks for. Reduced-motion fallback: this proposal IS the fallback design; every other proposal's RM story routes through it. No-JS behavior: pure CSS media query, identical with or without JS; JS effects (scramble, canvas, magnetics) remain fully disabled under RM via the existing matchMedia guards (Layout.astro:86, Hero.astro:72).
proposals.sketch: Replace the universal selector rule with a scoped policy. Keep: `transition-property: color, background-color, border-color, opacity, box-shadow` at durations <= 200ms (define --t-rm: 150ms and re-point --t-fast/--t inside the RM block). Kill: any transition/animation of transform, translate, scale, plus all infinite loops and scroll-linked movement — enumerate: .btn transform, .pcard/.gcard hover lift, magnetic vars, breathe, ping, pulse-dot, shimmer, nudge, circuit parallax/pulses, boot (already removed), name scramble (JS guard), scroll-driven proposals (add their animation: none here). Also listen for matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').addEventListener('change', ...) in Layout.astro so mid-session OS toggles stop the canvas and cursor effects without a reload. Record the policy as a decision record (motion = movement; feedback = opacity/color) in docs/decisions.md.

proposals.title: Nav and masthead micro-polish: center-origin underlines, scroll-spy crossfade, masthead power-on flicker
proposals.description: Three small coherence fixes. (1) Nav underlines grow from the left on both enter and exit (global.css:216-218), which reads as a directional artifact; growing from center on hover-in and shrinking to the side of the next hovered item — or simply center-origin both ways — feels engineered. (2) The scroll-spy aria-current swap (Layout.astro:128-142) snaps; giving the underline a shared spring transition makes the active indicator feel like it slides between items even though it's per-link (cheap version of a shared-element indicator). (3) On first load, the masthead 'rev.2026' and the accent '//' can do a single 2-frame LED flicker keyed off the hero @starting-style choreography — a 200ms grace note reinforcing the power-on narrative, played once, never looping. Also fix a real inconsistency: CSS styles nav__link[aria-current="true"] (global.css:217) but JS sets aria-current="location" (Layout.astro:135) — the active state styling currently never applies; any motion work here must fix that selector first. Reduced-motion fallback: underline transitions become instant color changes under the curated RM policy; the masthead flicker is a transform-free opacity blink but still a loop-adjacent effect, so disable it in the RM block. No-JS behavior: hover underlines are pure CSS and work; scroll-spy state simply never changes (as today); the flicker is CSS-only @starting-style so it plays without JS.
proposals.sketch: Fix selector to [aria-current="location"]. Center origin: `.nav__link::after { transform-origin: center; transform: scaleX(0) } .nav__link:hover::after, .nav__link[aria-current="location"]::after { transform: scaleX(1); transition-timing-function: var(--ease-spring-sm) }`. Flicker: `@starting-style { .masthead .rev { opacity: 0 } } .masthead .rev { transition: opacity 80ms steps(2, jump-none) 600ms }` — steps easing gives the fluorescent-tube blink with a single transition. For the sliding-indicator feel without JS layout math, add `transition: transform 300ms var(--ease-spring-sm)` on ::after and stagger nothing else; verify it under the RM policy (opacity-only fallback: swap transform for opacity in the RM block).

proposals.title: Two-metal color system: copper traces under the cyan signal
proposals.description: Everything decorative and everything interactive is currently the same cyan (#00E5FF), which flattens hierarchy and reads generic-techy. Real PCBs separate the passive copper layer from the live signal. Introduce a copper/ENIG-gold family for all static PCB scenery (circuit background traces, vias, pads, trace dividers, ticked corners, timeline rail) and reserve cyan strictly for live signal: pulses, hover states, links, the scroll rail fill, active spec values. The page instantly gains warmth, depth, and a defensible metaphor: copper = the board, cyan = current flowing through it.
proposals.sketch: In src/styles/tokens.css add --copper: #B87333; --copper-dim: #6E4A26; --copper-glow: rgba(184,115,51,0.14); --pad-gold: #D4A24E. Repoint --trace (line 32) from #16323D to a copper-dark like #3A2A1A-mixed value, or keep --trace for cyan contexts and swap the consumers: .circuit__base path / .circuit__via / .circuit__pad (global.css 445-447), .trace-div path (432), .tl-item::before (345), .ticked::before/::after (180-181) to copper tokens. Keep .circuit__pulse, .signal-rail__fill, all hover/focus states cyan. Verify contrast of copper on #0A0E14 stays decorative-only (no text). One evening of token surgery; zero JS, zero motion implications.

proposals.title: Authentic PCB grammar in the trace dividers: pads, annular rings, silkscreen refdes, per-section variants
proposals.description: TraceDivider.astro is one generic 600x24 path with a single dot — it reads as 'wavy line', not PCB. Upgrade it to real fab language: through-hole pads drawn as annular rings (outer circle + board-color hole), teardrop entries where the trace meets a pad, a test-point pad labeled 'TP1', and tiny silkscreen reference designators ('R7', 'C3') in 8px JetBrains Mono next to component footprints. Give the component a variant prop so each section gets a distinct divider — e.g. a differential pair (two parallel traces with length-matching serpentine) after Projects, a 4-bit bus with a junction after Skills. Recruiters who know hardware will recognize length-matching serpentines instantly; that is the memorable detail.
proposals.sketch: Extend src/components/TraceDivider.astro (line 5) with interface Props { variant?: 'single'|'diffpair'|'bus'|'serpentine' } and a small map of path sets. Annular ring = <circle r=4 fill=var(--copper)/> + <circle r=1.6 fill=var(--bg)/>. Refdes = <text> in font-family:var(--font-mono) font-size:7 fill:var(--silkscreen) (token already exists at tokens.css:33 and is unused). Keep the existing stroke-dasharray draw animation; set --len per variant. Serpentine path is just repeated 'l 8 -6 l 8 6' segments. Pass variants at the call sites in About.astro:45, Projects.astro:72, Footer.astro:7.

proposals.title: Datasheet 'Electrical Characteristics' table treatment for flagship card params
proposals.description: The section eyebrows already promise a datasheet ('// 04 — specifications', '// 05 — compliance & test') but the flagship param blocks are soft dotted-leader rows. Commit fully: render each flagship card's params as a genuine datasheet table — numbered caption ('TABLE 1-1 · OPERATING CHARACTERISTICS'), thin single-pixel row rules, uppercase mono column heads (PARAMETER / CONDITIONS / VALUE), tabular numerals, and a right-aligned 'NOTES' superscript on active rows. This is the highest-leverage 'premium theme execution' move because it converts decoration into information design that engineers and recruiters actually read.
proposals.sketch: In src/components/Projects.astro (params block, lines 40-49) swap the <dl class=spec> for a <table class=ds-table> with <caption>. In global.css add .ds-table { width:100%; border-collapse:collapse; font-size:var(--fs-small); } .ds-table caption { font-family:var(--font-mono); font-size:var(--fs-micro); letter-spacing:.14em; text-align:left; color:var(--muted); padding-bottom:var(--space-2); border-bottom:1px solid var(--border-bright); } .ds-table th { font-family:var(--font-mono); font-size:var(--fs-micro); text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--label); text-align:left; padding:.45em 0; } .ds-table td { border-top:1px solid var(--border); padding:.45em 0; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; } .ds-table td:last-child { text-align:right; color:var(--text); }. Keep the dotted-leader .spec style for hero/about/contact so the two idioms coexist. Wrap in overflow-x:auto on mobile. Pure HTML/CSS — no JS.

proposals.title: Schematic symbols as section markers
proposals.description: Each SectionHeader currently gets the same faint numeral. Give every scroll-stop a hand-drawn schematic symbol rendered in 1px silkscreen stroke beside the eyebrow: an IC package (DIP-8 with pin-1 dot) for About, a crystal oscillator for Projects, a timing/clock waveform for Experience, a resistor ladder for Skills, a zener diode for Certifications, an RF antenna for Contact. Six tiny SVGs, each ~15 lines, become the site's iconography system — instantly recognizable to any hardware person and unlike anything on a typical portfolio. The faint numeral stays; the symbol sits to the right of the rule.
proposals.sketch: Add optional symbol?: string prop to src/components/SectionHeader.astro (line 2) mapping to inline <svg class=section-head__sym viewBox='0 0 48 24'> definitions kept in a symbols.ts or inline map (stroke:var(--silkscreen); stroke-width:1; fill:none; the pin-1 dot fill:var(--accent)). Position: .section-head__sym { position:absolute; right:0; top:0.25rem; width:64px; opacity:.7; } inside .section-head__inner (SectionHeader.astro line 11), hidden under 720px. Wire the symbol name through the sections map in src/data/site.ts (line 315). Optionally reuse the same stroke-dasharray draw-on-scroll pattern already used by .trace-div (global.css 433) with the existing reduced-motion override.

proposals.title: IC-topmark hero treatment: name as a laser-etched chip marking
proposals.description: The hero name is a plain (if glitch-animated) H1. Add the one detail that makes it read as a component: directly beneath the name, a chip topmark block in mono — 'RAMU-ROY · REV.2026' / 'LOT: HYD-01 · ECE 8.3/10' / a date-code style 'DC:2026-26' — set in small letter-spaced JetBrains Mono at silkscreen gray, with a pin-1 indicator dot preceding the H1. Every embedded engineer has read a thousand chip topmarks; seeing a person presented as one is the kind of wit that gets a portfolio screenshotted and shared. Works with zero JS and replaces nothing — the existing ticker line moves into or below it.
proposals.sketch: In src/components/Hero.astro after the <h1> (line 15) add <div class=hero__topmark aria-hidden=true> with 2-3 <span> lines sourced from a new hero.topmark array in src/data/site.ts (near line 74, absorbing the existing ticker items). CSS: .hero__topmark { font-family:var(--font-mono); font-size:var(--fs-micro); letter-spacing:.22em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--silkscreen); line-height:1.9; }. Pin-1 dot: .hero h1::before { content:''; display:inline-block; width:.35em; height:.35em; border-radius:50%; background:var(--accent); margin-right:.3em; vertical-align:super; box-shadow:0 0 8px var(--glow); }. Optionally give the whole title block a faint rounded-rect 'package outline' border on ≥900px.

proposals.title: Mono type refinement: slashed zeros, tabular numerals globally, and architectural outline numerals
proposals.description: The data aesthetic deserves the last 10% of type craft. (1) JetBrains Mono ships a slashed zero via ss19/zero — enabling it makes every date, score, and spec value look like instrument output. (2) tabular-nums is applied piecemeal (.tnum, a few components); apply it to all mono contexts so ticker, dates, and topmarks never wobble. (3) The section numerals (--faint fill) currently read as smudges; render them as 1px outlined figures (transparent fill, text-stroke) so they become architectural grid furniture like drawing-frame numbers on a schematic sheet, and bump their size.
proposals.sketch: In src/styles/global.css extend the .mono helper (line 79) and .eyebrow with font-feature-settings:'zero' 1, 'ss19' 1; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; — or add a body-level rule scoped to var(--font-mono) users via a shared class. For numerals: .section-head__num (global.css line 109) → color:transparent; -webkit-text-stroke:1px var(--border-bright); paint-order:stroke; with an @supports not (-webkit-text-stroke:1px #000) fallback to the current --faint fill. Increase --fs-numeral (tokens.css line 98) top clamp to ~9rem and let it bleed slightly left of the container on ≥1100px (left:-0.35em) for asymmetry. Verify against the bundled Latin subset in src/styles/fonts.css (feature tables are included in the variable WOFF2).

proposals.title: Surface elevation ramp + film-grain to kill gradient banding
proposals.description: All cards share one flat recipe (var(--surface) + 1px border), and the two big fixed radial glows (body::after) band visibly on cheap displays. Two disciplined moves: (1) a real elevation system — level-1 surfaces get an inset top highlight (the classic 1px light edge that simulates machined metal), level-2 (hovered cards, nav) get a slightly lighter background from the existing --elevated tokens which are defined but underused; (2) a static SVG feTurbulence grain layer at ~2.5% opacity fixed over the background, which both hides banding and adds the analog 'photographed hardware' texture. Both are pure CSS, respect reduced-motion trivially (nothing moves), and cost one data-URI.
proposals.sketch: In global.css: give .spec-card, .pcard, .gcard, .cert, .contact__panel a shared box-shadow addition: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(230,237,243,0.045), var(--shadow-sm) — easiest by introducing a --edge-highlight token in tokens.css (shadow block, line 54) and appending it. Grain: body::after (line 51) gains a second background layer url("data:image/svg+xml,...feTurbulence type='fractalNoise' baseFrequency='0.9' numOctaves='2'...") with background-size:180px, or add a dedicated .grain fixed div in Layout.astro body (line 72) at opacity:.025; mix-blend-mode:overlay; pointer-events:none. Keep it OFF print (@media print already hides body::before/after at line 503). Total payload ~600 bytes.

proposals.title: Phosphor-green terminal voice for the boot intro and footer prompt
proposals.description: The boot/POST overlay and the footer 'rr@embedded:~$' colophon are terminal moments, but they currently speak the same cyan as the PCB layer, so the conceit is muted. Give the terminal voice its own channel: phosphor green (#3AFB77-family) text with a faint glow and a subtle CRT scanline background confined to the boot panel, plus the footer prompt line and the blinking caret. With copper (board), cyan (signal), and phosphor (terminal), the site has a coherent three-voice palette where each color means something — that is what separates an art-directed site from a themed one.
proposals.sketch: tokens.css: add --phosphor:#3AFB77; --phosphor-dim:#1E7A42; --phosphor-glow:rgba(58,251,119,0.25). global.css .boot (line 236): color the panel — .boot__panel { color:var(--phosphor-dim); } .boot__line .ok { color:var(--phosphor); text-shadow:0 0 8px var(--phosphor-glow); } .boot .caret { background:var(--phosphor); }. Scanlines on .boot only: background:linear-gradient(var(--bg-deep),var(--bg-deep)), repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, transparent 0 2px, rgba(58,251,119,0.02) 2px 3px). Footer: .footer__colophon (line 421) and its .accent + .caret switch to phosphor. Keep everything else cyan. Reduced-motion already stops the caret blink (line 519); scanlines are static so no motion concern.

proposals.title: Oscilloscope capture treatment for the stats band
proposals.description: The stats band is the weakest scroll-stop: four centered numbers with hairline dividers, identical to every SaaS landing page. Recast it as a scope screen: a graticule background (10x8 grid with center crosshair ticks, exactly like a Rigol/Tek display), each stat presented as a channel measurement — 'CH1' label chip in a distinct trace color, value in huge tabular numerals, measurement name below in scope-UI mono ('Meas: repos', 'Freq: protocols') — plus a 'TRIG'D' badge and '1M pts' style footer ticks. The count-up JS already exists; this is pure CSS dressing that converts a generic pattern into the single most screenshot-able moment on the page.
proposals.sketch: In src/components/Stats.astro (line 12) add a wrapping class stats--scope and per-stat CH{i+1}. global.css .stats (line 471): background-image of two repeating-linear-gradients at calc(100%/10) / calc(100%/8) using var(--grid-line), plus a center-line with slightly brighter ticks via linear-gradient layers; corner label .stats::before { content:'TRIG\2019D · AUTO'; position:absolute; top:8px; right:12px; font:...mono micro; color:var(--success); }. Channel chips: .stat__ch { font-family:var(--font-mono); font-size:var(--fs-micro); border:1px solid currentColor; padding:.1em .4em; border-radius:2px; } with nth-child colors — CH1 cyan (--accent), CH2 gold (--warn), CH3 phosphor (--success), CH4 violet (--accent-2), and the .stat__value inheriting each channel color instead of uniform cyan. All static CSS; count-up and reduced-motion behavior untouched (Layout.astro 303-345).

proposals.title: CAD-sheet grid exposure: drawing frame border with coordinate labels
proposals.description: Schematics and board layouts live inside a drawing frame — the lettered/numbered border grid (A-F, 1-8) with a title block. On ≥1200px, expose the site's own grid the same way: a fixed 1px frame inset from the viewport edge with coordinate letters along the left/right and numbers along the top, in silkscreen mono. The existing signal-rail node then travels along a frame that visibly belongs to a document, and the whole site reads as 'Sheet 1 of 1' of an engineering drawing. This is a composition move: it adds asymmetric micro-detail at the edges without touching content flow, and it costs nothing below desktop widths.
proposals.sketch: In src/layouts/Layout.astro body (near line 74, next to .signal-rail) add <div class=sheet-frame aria-hidden=true> containing spans for coords (A..E left, 1..6 top) or generate them in the template. CSS behind a @media (min-width:1200px) block: .sheet-frame { position:fixed; inset:10px; border:1px solid var(--border); pointer-events:none; z-index:1; } .sheet-frame span { position:absolute; font-family:var(--font-mono); font-size:9px; color:var(--faint); letter-spacing:.1em; } placed at percentage offsets; small 6px tick marks via repeating-linear-gradient on the frame's ::before along top/left edges. Add a bottom-right mini title block: 'RR-PORTFOLIO · SHEET 1/1 · REV 2026' in a 1px-bordered box, echoing the nav masthead. Ensure z-index sits below nav (100) and skip-link (200), and hide in @media print (global.css 500).

proposals.title: Logic-analyzer timeline: roles as signal channels with period ticks
proposals.description: The experience timeline is a stock vertical line with dots. Reframe it in the site's own language as a logic-analyzer/bus view: the rail becomes a copper bus with solder-junction pads at each role; each role gets a small waveform glyph next to the period — a high pulse spanning the employment window (rising edge at start, high level, falling edge or continuing-high with an arrow for the active role). Year ticks (2025 / 2026) annotate the rail in micro mono. It converts 'timeline' — the most cliched portfolio element — into a piece of the instrument metaphor, and the active role's still-high signal line is a genuinely elegant way to say 'present'.
proposals.sketch: In src/components/Experience.astro add a small inline SVG per tl-item next to .tl-item__date (line 14): viewBox='0 0 120 16', path like 'M0 13 H18 V3 H120' (rising edge then high) for active, '...V3 H96 V13 H120' (returns low) for ended roles; stroke:var(--accent) for active, var(--silkscreen) otherwise; stroke-width:1.5. Rail upgrade in global.css: .tl-item::before (line 345) width:2px background:var(--copper-dim); .tl-item__node (347) becomes a square pad (border-radius:2px) with an inner hole dot, matching the annular-ring language from the divider proposal. Year ticks: absolutely positioned <span class=tl-year> elements or a dt-style label at each item, font-size:9-10px mono, left:-2.6rem on ≥900px. Optional draw-on-scroll via existing stroke-dasharray + .in-view pattern with the reduced-motion override at global.css 513.

proposals.title: Skip the light theme; invest in a 'datasheet paper' print/PDF stylesheet instead
proposals.description: A toggleable light theme would cost a full token audit (40+ color tokens, glows, canvas colors hardcoded in Hero.astro JS at rgba(0,229,255,...)), require JS-persisted state that violates the no-JS spirit, and dilute the dark-CAD identity that IS the brand — meta name=color-scheme is already committed to dark (Layout.astro line 42). The one context where light matters is paper: recruiters print or PDF portfolios. Upgrade the existing minimal print block into a true datasheet-paper rendition — white sheet, black text, thin rules, the section numbering and TABLE captions retained, mono headers, a printed title block ('RAMU ROY — DATASHEET — REV 2026') and page footer. Ctrl+P then becomes a feature you can mention: 'the site prints as its own datasheet.'
proposals.sketch: Expand @media print in src/styles/global.css (line 500): re-declare the core tokens inside :root { --bg:#fff; --text:#111; --accent:#000; --border:#999; ... } so component CSS follows automatically instead of per-selector overrides; force .pcard/.spec-card { border:1px solid #000; box-shadow:none; border-radius:0; }; open all <details> for print via details[open]-equivalent — add a tiny beforeprint listener OR simpler, [class] details { display:block } trick won't open them, so instead print-expand with details > ul { display:block !important } plus summary { list-style:none } (test in Chromium print preview); add running header via position:fixed top block. Also expose an explicit 'PRINT DATASHEET' ghost button in Contact.astro (near line 48) — an <a href='javascript:window.print()' is JS-dependent, so use a <button onclick> enhancement that is hidden without JS via html.js gating already established (global.css 99). Verdict recorded as a decision entry in docs/decisions.md following D-013's format.

proposals.title: Add a measurable-outcomes row to every flagship project (numbers, not adjectives)
proposals.description: No project on the site has a single quantified result. The flagship params (src/data/site.ts:133-139, 158-164, 183-189) list platforms and buses, and the only 'Result' rows are qualitative ('Live @ Tata Steel BlueScope', '100% on-device'). A firmware hiring manager screening in 30 seconds looks for numbers that prove the candidate measured their system: latency budgets, update rates, sizes, error rates. Their absence is the single biggest gap between this site and a top-tier embedded portfolio. Also add explicit role/scope: nothing says whether he was the sole firmware engineer on the anti-collision system (the resume's 'Developed' implies yes) or team size on eOS.
proposals.sketch: Extend the Flagship type in src/data/site.ts:101-115 with metrics: {k,v}[] and roleLine: string, render them as a second highlighted <dl class="spec"> block in src/components/Projects.astro:40-49 (pure static HTML, no JS). Concrete numbers to collect from the actual systems: Anti-Collision — UWB ranging rate (Hz), worst-case zone-decision-to-relay-trip latency (ms), node/crane count, months in production, operating range (m); eOS — WIC image size (MB), cold-boot time (s), A/B OTA swap+verify time, recipe count in meta-eos; Voice — wake-word false-accepts/hr and FRR %, Whisper real-time factor on Pi 5, barge-in interrupt latency (ms). Add roleLine like 'Sole firmware engineer, 6-month engagement' to the anti-collision card and 'One of N engineers; own OTA, voice, sensor fusion' to eOS.

proposals.title: Give each section a distinct job — stop telling the same resume three times
proposals.description: About paragraph 2 (src/data/site.ts:88) is a prose restatement of the Radiogeet experience entry (site.ts:260-267) and flagship card 2 (site.ts:147-166); About paragraph 3 (site.ts:89) restates the Elipse entry and flagship 1 almost clause-for-clause ('BitBake PR bumps, AUTOREV pinning, IPK packaging' appears 3 times on one page: lines 127, 89-implied, 245). A recruiter reading top-to-bottom experiences déjà vu, and the site adds nothing over the PDF resume it links to. The single page should complement the PDF: Experience = terse scope/dates/role; Projects = deep technical detail with evidence; About = 2-3 sentences of narrative voice and what he wants next — not a third copy of the bullets.
proposals.sketch: In src/data/site.ts cut about.paragraphs (86-90) to one short paragraph (the seams-between-layers framing from paragraph 1, plus one sentence on what role he's looking for). Trim experience[].highlights (244-251) to 3 bullets max per role, dropping any bullet whose content already lives in a flagship card, and end each with 'Full detail: FIG. 01/02' anchor links to the project cards (#projects works without JS). Keep flagship highlights (127-131, 152-156) as the canonical deep version. Net effect: page gets ~30% shorter and each scroll-stop delivers new information.

proposals.title: Ship visual evidence: hardware photos, KiCad renders, and inline SVG architecture diagrams
proposals.description: The site contains zero images of actual work — no bench photos, no PCB renders, no scope traces, no block diagrams — for a candidate whose pitch is 'I build hardware.' Claims like 'dual-core firmware: core 1 UWB ranging, core 2 zone logic' (site.ts:152) beg for a one-glance block diagram, and the six featured PCB/hardware grid cards (site.ts:206-212) are text-only when KiCad produces free 3D renders. Embedded recruiters treat photos of real rigged-up hardware as the strongest authenticity signal; their absence makes the page read like it could have been written without touching a board.
