proposals.title: Replace Google Drive cert links with official NPTEL verification URLs and demote the score gauges
proposals.description: Both certification links (src/data/site.ts:299-300) point to personal Google Drive files — a recruiter clicking through gets an unverifiable scan behind a consumer share link that can silently break or prompt for access. NPTEL certificates carry an official verification URL (nptel.ac.in / archive QR endpoint with the certificate number) that proves authenticity in one click. Separately, the animated 85%/88% gauges (Certifications.astro:17-22) give two online courses more visual ceremony than the Tata Steel production deployment gets — a weighting a screener will notice.
proposals.sketch: Swap url values in site.ts:299-300 for the official NPTEL verify links printed on the certificates (format: https://archive.nptel.ac.in/content/noc/.../Certificate/... or the QR verify URL) and change the link label in Certifications.astro:24 from 'view certificate' to 'verify ↗'. Compress the section: drop the gauge bars, render each cert as one spec row (title · NPTEL 2025 · 85% · verify) inside the existing education spec-card in Experience.astro:34-46, and retire the standalone section 05 — shortening the page and removing a section whose visual weight exceeds its signal.

proposals.title: Replace the vanity stats strip with proof stats
proposals.description: The four stats (src/components/Stats.astro:5-10) are '19 GitHub repos · 18 projects · 12 protocols · 5 programming languages' — all volume counts, two of them (protocols, languages) obvious padding that experienced screeners read as junior-résumé inflation. The strip occupies the most valuable slot on the page (directly under the hero) and currently spends it on numbers no hiring manager cares about, while the genuinely rare facts — production safety system, full custom distro, fully on-device voice — are buried below.
proposals.sketch: Rework the stats array in Stats.astro (keeping the D-009 derived-data pattern) to lead with outcomes: '1 safety system live in production', 'N months running at Tata Steel BlueScope' (derive from a deployment date constant in site.ts so it never goes stale), '3 stack layers owned — PCB / firmware / distro', '0 cloud dependencies in the voice pipeline'. Keep the counter animation and no-JS fallback exactly as-is; only the data changes. Retire the hardcoded githubRepoCount (site.ts:16) from the strip so an externally-observed number can't drift.

proposals.title: Hide sub-10 star counts and fix the overclaiming 'Object Detection' title
proposals.description: The flagship anti-collision card displays '★ 1' (site.ts:166, rendered at Projects.astro:66) and the featured grid shows '★ 3' — printing tiny star counts actively advertises low GitHub traction and, because the grid sorts by stars (Projects.astro:7), puts a hobby power supply above the RTOS work. Separately, 'Object Detection over SPI' (site.ts:213) describes an IR proximity sensor — 'object detection' reads as a computer-vision claim, and a screener who clicks the repo and finds an IR sensor logs it as inflation, which then taints the genuinely strong claims elsewhere on the page.
proposals.sketch: In Projects.astro, gate star rendering behind a threshold (stars >= 10) or drop the star field entirely from cards, and sort the featured grid by a curated order field or by category (Hardware/PCB → Firmware/RTOS → IoT) instead of stars. Rename the site.ts:213 entry to 'IR Presence Detection over SPI (ESP32 ↔ Arduino)' — or unfeature it — and unfeature 'Fire Detection System' (site.ts:214, an MQ-2 Arduino starter project) so every featured tile survives a click-through by a senior firmware engineer. Uses the existing featured flag mechanism from decision D-010.

proposals.title: Cut contact friction: persistent nav CTA, prefilled mailto, plain-language button labels
proposals.description: Reaching contact info requires either a full-page scroll or knowing to open the nav menu — the sticky nav (Nav.astro:10-17) has five section links plus GitHub but no email and no CV, so the two actions a convinced recruiter takes both live at the extreme bottom of a long page. The contact CTA is labelled 'OPEN MAILTO' (Contact.astro:47), which is developer-speak; and the bare mailto forces the recruiter to compose from scratch. Every extra second of friction on a 100-portfolios-a-month desk loses replies.
proposals.sketch: Add a visually distinct <a class="btn btn-primary" href="mailto:..."> as the last nav item in Nav.astro (styled small, always visible on desktop, inside the existing mobile menu) plus the CV link. Change the mailto everywhere to mailto:royramu694429@gmail.com?subject=Embedded%20role%20%E2%80%94%20reaching%20out%20from%20your%20site so replies are pre-triaged. Rename 'OPEN MAILTO' to 'EMAIL ME'. All pure HTML — zero JS, zero CSP impact. Optionally add an obfuscation-free vCard (.vcf in public/) link next to the copy buttons for one-tap contact saving.

proposals.title: Add a logistics block: availability date, relocation, remote/onsite, notice period, graduation status
proposals.description: The site says 'AVAILABLE' (site.ts:20-21, hero keySpecs line 80) but answers none of the questions a recruiter must resolve before reaching out: available from when? Open to relocation within India / abroad? Remote or onsite? Notice period at Elipse (the role is 'May 2026 – Present', i.e. current employment — 'available' while employed needs one clarifying line or it reads as contradictory)? Has the 2026 B.Tech actually been conferred? Ambiguity here costs real outreach: recruiters skip candidates whose logistics they'd have to interview to learn.
proposals.sketch: Add a logistics object to src/data/site.ts (availableFrom, noticePeriod, workMode: 'onsite/hybrid/remote', relocation: 'yes — within India / open to visa sponsorship', degreeConferred: '2026') and render it as three extra spec rows in the Contact panel dl (Contact.astro:16-43) and one consolidated row in hero keySpecs. Reconcile the 'AVAILABLE' pill with current Elipse employment explicitly — e.g. 'open to embedded roles · notice period 30 days' — so the status is a fact, not a puzzle.

proposals.title: Publish a verifiable public artifact for the two closed-source flagships
proposals.description: Two of three flagship cards end in 'Elipse · no public repo' / 'part of eOS' (site.ts:140, 190). For an early-career candidate the flagships are the entire hiring case, and right now the strongest work is unverifiable while the verifiable repos are Arduino starters — exactly backwards from a screener's perspective. The wake-word pipeline (Google speech_embedding backbone → PyTorch head → ONNX → tract) is generic enough to open-source without touching Elipse IP, and a written architecture case study of eOS costs nothing proprietary.
proposals.sketch: Create two public repos and link them from site.ts: (1) a standalone wake-word training + tract-inference repo — training script, ONNX export, a Rust crate running inference, and a README with benchmark table (model size, FAR/hr, FRR, inference ms on Pi 5) — set as flagship 3's repo field replacing noRepoNote; (2) an 'eos-architecture-notes' repo or a long-form README: block diagram, recipe-layer layout, A/B OTA flow, D-Bus interface sketches (names are already public on this site at site.ts:128), linked from flagship 1 as 'REF → architecture write-up'. Pin both on the GitHub profile so the profile's above-the-fold matches the site's flagships.

proposals.title: Reorder for the 30-second screen and fix the hero's weakest-first signal ordering
proposals.description: The scan order is Hero → Stats → About (three dense paragraphs) → Projects (index.astro:13-20): a screener hits a wall of prose before any project card. Meanwhile the hero ticker (site.ts:74) leads with 'cgpa 8.3' — a grade — before the production deployment, and CGPA appears four times on one page (ticker, keySpecs:77, about glance:94, education:304), which over-indexes on student identity for someone with a system running at Tata Steel. The strongest fact should be the first fact everywhere.
proposals.sketch: In src/pages/index.astro move <Projects /> above <About /> (with proposal 2's shortened About this reads naturally as work-first, story-second). In site.ts:74 reorder the ticker to lead with proof: 'deployed @ Tata Steel BlueScope', 'custom Yocto distro in active dev', '100% on-device voice', then tooling; delete 'cgpa 8.3' and the repo count from it. Remove CGPA from about.glance (line 94), keeping it only in hero keySpecs and Education. Renumber the section eyebrows (sections object, site.ts:315-322) to match the new order — the '// 0N —' labels are data-driven so this is a one-file change.

proposals.title: Align claim verbs with tenure: 'Architected' after two months reads as inflation
proposals.description: The Elipse role started May 2026 (site.ts:239) — about ten weeks before today — yet the first highlight claims 'Architected a Yocto/OpenEmbedded distro' (site.ts:245) and the summary says 'Building eOS'. The PDF resume the site links says 'Contributing to a Yocto Project / OpenEmbedded-based custom embedded Linux operating system.' A recruiter who opens both (they do) sees the site outbidding the resume, and dated overclaims are among the fastest credibility killers in embedded hiring, where reference checks with small companies are easy.
proposals.sketch: Edit site.ts:242-250 to scope-honest verbs that are still strong: 'Own the OTA/build pipeline, the Rust sensor-fusion framework, and the voice subsystem within eOS' — ownership of subsystems is credible at 2 months and actually more informative than 'architected the distro'. Apply the same pass to flagship 1's highlights (site.ts:127-130): keep 'Authored recipes', 'Built the voice subsystem', change any whole-system authorship verb where the resume says 'contribute'. Ensure the resume PDF and the site tell the same story at the same altitude — the site may add detail and evidence, never bigger verbs.

proposals.title: UART console easter egg behind the footer prompt
proposals.description: The footer already renders 'rr@embedded:~$ built with astro' with a blinking caret (src/components/Footer.astro:14) — a working terminal is the natural payoff of that motif. Clicking the prompt (or pressing the backtick key) opens a small monospace console panel that accepts real commands: help, whoami, uname -a, ls projects/, cat resume.txt (prints a plaintext resume and offers the PDF link), cat /etc/os-release (eOS branding), dmesg (replays the boot log), contact, reboot (re-runs the BootIntro overlay), clear, exit. To a senior engineer this reads as impressive rather than gimmicky precisely because the command set is terse, accurate, and in-universe (ESP-IDF/Linux-flavored output, correct exit codes, 'command not found' for garbage). No-JS degradation is clean: the trigger affordance is only attached by JS (same pattern as .boot in global.css:236, hidden until script succeeds), so no-JS users just see the existing static colophon line. Fully static-host compatible — zero network calls, satisfies the same-origin CSP because Astro hashes component <script> tags. Reduced motion: no typewriter effect, output prints instantly.
proposals.sketch: New src/components/Terminal.astro included from Layout.astro. Markup: a <div class='term' role='region' aria-label='Interactive console' hidden> containing a scrollable <output> log and an <input> with a mono prompt prefix; styled with existing tokens (--code-bg, --accent, --font-mono, .ticked corners). JS (vanilla, in the component <script> so Astro CSP-hashes it): command table as a Record<string, () => string | string[]>, importing profile/flagship/gridProjects from src/data/site.ts at build time via define:vars or by inlining a JSON blob in frontmatter so answers stay in sync with the data model (D-009). Wire triggers: footer colophon gets cursor:pointer + aria-expanded via JS only; keydown listener for '`' when no input is focused. 'reboot' dispatches sessionStorage.removeItem('rr_boot') then re-inserts the BootIntro markup or simply location.reload(). Respect prefers-reduced-motion: skip the per-character setTimeout typing and append lines synchronously. Keep focus trapped only while the panel is open; Escape closes and restores focus (mirror the mobile-menu handling in Layout.astro:233). Add a one-line hint 'type help' as the first log entry. ~150 lines of JS, no dependencies.

proposals.title: Protocol-decode trace dividers (I2C / SPI / UART waveforms with decode annotations)
proposals.description: TraceDivider.astro currently draws a generic PCB trace (src/components/TraceDivider.astro:5). Replace the section dividers with logic-analyzer-style waveforms of *correctly decoded* protocol transactions — e.g. the About divider shows an I2C write (START, addr 0x3C W, ACK, data byte, STOP) with SDA/SCL rails and tiny decode labels; the Projects divider shows a UART frame at 8N1 transmitting the byte for 'R'; the Skills divider shows SPI MOSI/MISO/SCK/CS. A senior embedded engineer will instantly check whether the start bit, ACK timing, and MSB/LSB order are right — getting it correct is a credibility signal no amount of copy can buy, and it directly illustrates the protocols list in src/data/site.ts:296. Feasibility is excellent: the site already generates deterministic SVG procedurally in Astro frontmatter (Circuit.astro:1-47), so waveforms can be computed at build time from an actual byte value — provably correct by construction. No-JS/reduced-motion: identical to the current trace-div pattern — the full static SVG is the default state, stroke-dashoffset draw-on-scroll only activates under .js.reveal-ready (global.css:432-439), and prefers-reduced-motion already forces stroke-dashoffset:0 (global.css:520).
proposals.sketch: Extend TraceDivider.astro with a props interface: { protocol: 'i2c'|'spi'|'uart', byte?: number, addr?: number }. In frontmatter, write a small pure function that converts a byte into an array of {t, level} edges per channel (for UART: idle-high, start bit low, 8 data bits LSB-first, stop bit; for I2C: SDA transitions only while SCL low, 9th clock ACK), then emit <path d='M...'> step waveforms (H/V commands only, like Circuit.astro) plus <text> decode labels ('S', '0x3C', 'W', 'ACK', 'P') in --font-mono at --fs-micro fill=var(--silkscreen). Two or three horizontal rails 8px apart inside the existing 24px-tall viewBox (bump to ~48px for two channels). Keep --len set to the computed path length so the existing draw animation works unchanged. Pass different protocol/byte per call site (About.astro:45, Projects.astro:72, Footer.astro:7). Add <title> in the SVG ('I2C write to 0x3C, ACKed') so hover shows the decode; keep aria-hidden since it is decorative. Zero JS added.

proposals.title: Replace the generic constellation hero canvas with an oscilloscope/logic-analyzer scene
proposals.description: The current hero canvas (src/components/Hero.astro:74-153) is a particles-and-lines constellation — the single most template-looking element on an otherwise domain-specific page; every framework portfolio has one. Replace it with an oscilloscope rendering: a faint graticule (already echoed by the body blueprint grid), one or two phosphor-glow traces showing a live UART TX line 'transmitting' the hero ticker strings byte-by-byte at a plausible timebase, with scope UI chrome (CH1 3.3V/div, 100µs/div, trigger arrow at the start bit) drawn in the corner. Cursor interaction: pointer position becomes a pair of measurement cursors showing Δt/ΔV readouts, replacing the constellation's mouse-attraction. This converts decoration into proof-of-domain and pairs with the protocol dividers. Degradation story is already solved by the existing structure: canvas is aria-hidden, skipped entirely under prefers-reduced-motion (Hero.astro:77), paused off-screen by IntersectionObserver, and no-JS users lose nothing content-wise. Add a static CSS graticule on .hero so even no-JS/reduced-motion visitors get the scope aesthetic without motion.
proposals.sketch: Rewrite the canvas script in Hero.astro. Precompute the waveform: encode each ticker string ('yocto', 'rust', ...) to UART frames (LSB-first, start/stop bits) as a step function; render with ctx.lineTo steps scrolling right-to-left at ~60px/s, stroke rgba(0,229,255,0.9) with shadowBlur=8 shadowColor=var glow for phosphor bloom, plus a dimmer persistence pass (draw previous frame at globalAlpha 0.35 instead of clearRect for phosphor decay — cap DPR at 2 as now). Graticule: 10x8 divisions via two nested loops of 1px lines at rgba(124,140,255,0.06), center crosshair dashed. Decode overlay: when a full byte scrolls past the trigger point, fillText the ASCII char above the frame in --font-mono. Cursor measurement: reuse the existing pointermove handler; draw two vertical dashed lines at mouse.x±40 and a readout box 'Δt=347µs  1/Δt=2.88kHz'. Keep the IO pause logic and reduce guard verbatim. Static fallback: add a .hero::before repeating-linear-gradient graticule at low opacity in global.css so the scene reads scope-like even when the canvas never starts. ~180 lines, no deps.

proposals.title: Real eOS boot log for the intro overlay, shared with the terminal's dmesg/reboot
proposals.description: The boot intro currently prints three generic lines ('mounting profile rev.2026') from src/data/site.ts:51-55. Swap in a condensed but *authentic* eOS boot transcript built from strings that exist in his actual stack: U-Boot on the Pi 5, kernel version, systemd reaching eos-core.target, 'rauc: booted slot A (rootfs.0), marking good', 'mosquitto: TLS listener :8883 up', 'eos-voice: KWS model loaded (tract, 1.2MB ONNX)'. Every line becomes a resume bullet a technical screener absorbs in the first 1.5 seconds — the intro stops being a loading gag and starts being content. Anyone who has brought up a Yocto board will recognize the cadence; anyone who hasn't still reads 'this person builds operating systems'. Effort is small: it is a data change plus minor timing tuning, and the accessibility/lifecycle hardening (D-007) is already done. Keep total duration ≤1.6s by batching lines (3 groups with 0.18s stagger) rather than one-by-one. No-JS: overlay never shows (already the case, global.css:236). Reduced motion: already bypassed (BootIntro.astro:39). The same string array feeds the terminal's dmesg command and reboot replay, so it is written once (D-009).
proposals.sketch: Extend bootLines in src/data/site.ts to ~10 lines with a {text, status?: 'ok', delayGroup} shape; update BootIntro.astro to render kernel-style timestamps ([    0.0421]) in --muted with the message in --text-secondary and [ ok ] in --accent (the split logic at BootIntro.astro:8 already handles the ok token — generalize it to the typed shape per D-008, no set:html). Set animation-delay from delayGroup instead of index so 10 lines land in 3 beats; keep the 1300ms auto-dismiss timer but bump to ~1700ms, keeping the skip button and Escape path unchanged. Export the same array for Terminal.astro's dmesg. Verify strings with Ramu for employer-confidentiality before shipping (eOS is Elipse-internal); use only facts already published on the page.

proposals.title: Flash / partition-map explorer for the flagship cards (RAUC A/B and ESP32 OTA layouts)
proposals.description: Both flagship stories are fundamentally about memory layout — eOS ships A/B RAUC OTA on a WIC image, and the anti-collision firmware lives in an ESP-IDF OTA partition scheme — yet the cards describe this only in prose (src/data/site.ts:127-130, 152). Add a proportional, datasheet-style partition bar to each card: for eOS, the SD image (boot FAT32 → rootfs slot A → rootfs slot B → data, with 'booted / marked good' highlighting slot A); for FIG.02, the standard ESP32-S3 table (nvs @0x9000, otadata, ota_0, ota_1, spiffs) with hex offsets and sizes. Hovering or focusing a segment reveals offset/size/purpose in a spec-row popover; on touch/no-JS every segment's label is simply visible below the bar. This is the 'register-map explorer' idea landed where it is honest: ESP-IDF partition tables and RAUC slot layouts are public conventions, so nothing proprietary is invented, unlike a fabricated register map. It is pure HTML/CSS (flexbox bar with width percentages, <details>/:hover for the drill-down), so the no-JS and reduced-motion stories are trivially perfect, and it strongly differentiates from portfolios that only list buzzwords. Senior-engineer read: authentic — this is exactly the diagram they draw on whiteboards.
proposals.sketch: New src/components/PartitionMap.astro taking { segments: {name, offset, size, note, active?}[] } with data added to each Flagship entry in site.ts. Render an <figure> with a flex row of <div class='pmap__seg'> whose flex-grow is proportional to log-scaled size (linear scale makes nvs invisible next to app slots — use flex-grow: max(1, log2(sizeKB))), borders var(--border), active slot gets var(--accent) top border + pill--production styling. Under the bar, a .spec dl reusing the existing dotted-leader rows (global.css:161) listing offset (mono, tabular-nums, 0x-prefixed) / size / purpose; on wide screens hide the dl and show per-segment popovers via .pmap__seg:hover .pmap__tip / :focus-within (segments are tabindex=0 with aria-describedby), on narrow screens or no hover always show the dl (@media (hover: none)). Optional JS-free polish: an animated 'OTA write' shimmer across the inactive slot using the existing pulse-dot/flow keyframes, disabled under prefers-reduced-motion via the existing global override (global.css:514). Place inside .pcard__params region of Projects.astro:40.

proposals.title: Interactive PCB layer viewer from his real KiCad boards (CSS-only layer toggles)
proposals.description: Five of his GitHub repos are real KiCad boards with gerbers (Transformerless PSU — his most-starred repo, LM2596 buck, AMS1117 regulator). Exporting one board's layers to SVG and embedding it as an interactive layer-toggle viewer (F.Cu / B.Cu / silkscreen / mask / drill checkboxes, like KiCad's layer manager) puts an actual engineering artifact on the page instead of a description of one. Crucially this can be 100% CSS: checkbox-hack layer toggles (<input type=checkbox> + sibling selectors driving SVG group visibility) work with JavaScript disabled, are keyboard accessible for free, and cost zero runtime. This is the single most 'show, don't tell' feature possible for the Hardware/PCB claim, and unlike simulated scope traces it is verifiably his own work — a recruiter can click through to the same repo. Effort is L because it needs one-time asset work: exporting clean SVGs with kicad-cli, flattening to the site palette, and svgo-minifying to keep the page fast; but there is no build-pipeline dependency (commit the processed SVG to the repo). Degrades perfectly: no-JS fully functional, reduced-motion irrelevant (no motion), static hosting trivial (inline SVG, CSP-clean).
proposals.sketch: One-time: clone ramuroy/Transformerless-Power-Supply, run `kicad-cli pcb export svg --layers F.Cu,B.Cu,F.SilkS,Edge.Cuts --exclude-drawing-sheet`, merge layers into one SVG with <g id='layer-fcu'> groups, recolor to tokens (copper=var(--accent-deep) at 0.8, silk=var(--silkscreen), edge=var(--border-bright)), svgo it (target <60KB gzipped; simplify pours if needed). New src/components/PcbViewer.astro: a .ticked spec-card containing the inline SVG plus a fieldset of styled checkboxes ('F.Cu', 'B.Cu', 'Silkscreen'), CSS like `.pcb:has(#l-fcu:not(:checked)) .layer-fcu { opacity: 0; }` (`:has` is baseline-supported; fallback: order checkboxes as preceding siblings and use ~). Default all layers on so the no-CSS/reader view is complete. Add a dimension callout ('54 × 38 mm, 2-layer') in mono and a REF → github link matching .pcard__ref styling. Mount it inside the featured Transformerless PSU grid card or as a full-width exhibit between flagship grid and 'selected on github'. Transition opacity var(--t-fast); no keyframe animation so reduced-motion needs nothing.

proposals.title: Representative MODBUS RTU / relay I-O map panel in the anti-collision card
proposals.description: FIG.02's strongest claim — driving industrial relays over MODBUS RTU to stop a crane — is exactly the kind of claim engineers probe in interviews. A compact, datasheet-style I/O map makes it concrete: an 8-row coil table (coil 0x0001 'ZONE-A HALT relay', function 0x05 Write Single Coil, slave addr, 9600 8E1) plus one annotated request/response frame ('01 05 00 01 FF 00 DD FA' with bytes color-coded: addr / func / coil / value / CRC-16). Feasibility: pure build-time HTML in the existing <details class='pcard__details'> disclosure (Projects.astro:51), which already works without JS. The CRC in the example frame must be computed correctly (trivially done in frontmatter) — engineers will check it, and a correct CRC-16/MODBUS is a delightful hidden proof of competence. Important honesty constraint: label it 'representative map' and use generic zone names, since the real Tata Steel register assignments are the employer's; a fabricated 'actual' map would be both a confidentiality risk and detectable as fake. With that framing it reads as strong documentation instinct, not gimmick.
proposals.sketch: Add a modbus field to the FIG.02 entry in src/data/site.ts: { slave: 1, coils: [{addr: 1, name 'ZONE-A HALT', fc: '0x05'}...], exampleWrite: {coil: 1, value: true} }. In Projects.astro (or a small ModbusMap.astro), compute CRC-16/MODBUS in frontmatter (~10-line polynomial 0xA001 loop over the 6 message bytes) and render: (1) a .spec dl of coils using the existing dotted-leader rows; (2) the frame as a row of <span class='byte'> chips in --font-mono with a color legend underneath — addr=var(--accent-2), func=var(--warn), data=var(--text), crc=var(--success) — each byte with a title attribute and a visible legend line for touch/no-hover. Wrap in a second <details> ('I/O map') under the existing 'Engineering detail' one so the card doesn't grow by default. No JS; hover styling only via CSS. Run the wording past Ramu/Radiogeet for confidentiality before merging.

proposals.title: Voice-pipeline signal-flow diagram with latency budget, animated with the existing pulse system
proposals.description: The On-Device Voice Subsystem card (FIG.03) describes a pipeline — ESP32 satellite mics → best-source fusion → KWS (tract/ONNX) → Whisper STT → intent → Piper TTS with barge-in — that is begging to be a block diagram instead of four bullets. Render it as a build-time SVG: mono-labeled blocks connected by PCB-style traces, each edge annotated with what flows across it (16kHz PCM frames, mel spectrogram 40×61, token stream) and a per-stage latency label, with an animated current pulse flowing along the path reusing the exact .circuit__pulse stroke-dasharray technique already in global.css:448 (and therefore already silenced by the prefers-reduced-motion override at global.css:522). Barge-in is drawn as a feedback trace from mic back to the TTS block labeled 'cancel'. Impressive-vs-gimmicky: block diagrams with honest data-rate annotations are the lingua franca of embedded design reviews — this reads as senior. No-JS: the full static SVG shows (animation is CSS-only, and even without it the diagram is complete). Effort is genuinely small because the visual system (traces, vias, pulses, mono labels, silkscreen color) already exists in Circuit.astro and tokens.css.
proposals.sketch: New src/components/PipelineDiagram.astro generating an SVG (viewBox ~760×180) in frontmatter from a typed node list: [{id:'mics', label:'ESP32 sat. mics ×N'}, {id:'fusion', label:'best-source fusion'}, {id:'kws', label:'KWS · tract'}, {id:'stt', label:'Whisper'}, {id:'tts', label:'Piper'}] with edges [{from,to,label:'16kHz PCM',lat:'~10ms'}]. Blocks: <rect> with rx=4, stroke var(--border-bright), fill var(--surface); labels in --font-mono at 11px fill var(--text-secondary); edges as H/V/45° paths stroke var(--trace) with a .circuit__pulse-classed overlay path per edge (stagger --delay so one pulse appears to travel the whole chain). Latency labels in var(--accent-text). Place inside FIG.03's card between description and params in Projects.astro, sized max-width:100% with an overflow-x:auto wrapper for narrow screens. aria: role='img' with an aria-label sentence describing the chain (it carries content, unlike the background circuit). Reduced motion and no-JS need zero extra work.

proposals.title: Print-to-datasheet mode: the page prints as a component datasheet
proposals.description: A print stylesheet already exists (global.css:500-508) but it just neutralizes the theme. Upgrade it so Ctrl+P yields a genuine-looking component datasheet: header block 'RR-2026 · Embedded Systems Engineer · Rev 2026-A', a 'Device Overview' (about), 'Electrical Characteristics'-style skills table (the .spec dotted-leader rows already look like datasheet parameter tables), 'Applications' (projects), 'Ordering Information' (contact — the section eyebrow at src/data/site.ts:321 already jokes 'contact & ordering info', so the punchline is pre-installed). Recruiters print or PDF portfolios constantly; handing them an artifact that looks like an ST/TI datasheet is memorable, useful (it becomes a leave-behind), and costs zero runtime bytes for screen visitors. This is one of the few showmanship ideas with literally no JS, no motion, no hosting implications — pure CSS @media print. Gimmick check: the datasheet-resume trope lands well when typography is disciplined and jokes are minimal (one 'Absolute Maximum Ratings' row max); keep it 95% straight documentation. Discoverability: add a small 'print datasheet ⎙' link in the footer (works no-JS — it can be an <a href='javascript:print()'> replaced by a JS-attached button; for no-JS just omit it, since Ctrl+P still works).
proposals.sketch:
Extend the @media print block in src/styles/global.css: switch body to a compact serif-free two-column layout for the skills/params sections (columns: 2 on .skills__grid), add datasheet chrome via body::before (fixed top rule with 'RR-2026 — PRELIMINARY — Ramu Roy' in mono 8pt) and @page { margin: 18mm; } with page numbers via @page @bottom-right if supported (fallback: static footer line). Force .pcard__details[open] equivalent: details { display:block } summary { display:none } details > ul { display:block !important } so engineering detail bullets print (details content is print-hidden today — check and fix). Hide interactive-only chrome (copy buttons, terminal, ticker). Add print-only elements (

) for the header block and doc-number footer, display:none on screen. Add a footer button (JS-attached, hidden no-JS) calling window.print() labeled 'print datasheet'. Test with Chrome print preview + `--headless --print-to-pdf` for regression checking in scripts/check-build.mjs if desired.

proposals.title: View-source and DevTools console signature advertising the easter eggs
proposals.description: Technical recruiters' engineers (and curious seniors) habitually open DevTools on a portfolio this styled. Right now they find nothing personal. Add (1) an ASCII-art HTML comment at the top of <body> — a small PCB/logo mark plus 'hand-rolled Astro, zero trackers, try the console' — and (2) a styled console.log boot banner ('eos-console v1.0 — type portfolio.help()') exposing a tiny window.portfolio object with help(), resume() (opens the PDF), and contact() returning the email. This is a low-cost, well-loved convention (GitHub, Stripe, Vercel all do it) that also solves discoverability for the terminal easter egg. It cannot be gimmicky because only people who go looking find it. No-JS story: the HTML comment is still there in source; the console part simply doesn't run. Zero visual or performance impact; CSP-safe since it lives in the existing hashed inline script in Layout.astro.
proposals.sketch: In src/layouts/Layout.astro: add the ASCII comment as a static HTML comment right after <body> (keep under ~15 lines / 600 bytes; compressHTML preserves comments only if configured — verify Astro's compressHTML doesn't strip comments; if it does, emit via set:html on a Fragment or place it before the doctype where it survives). Console banner in the existing main <script>: console.log('%c rr@embedded ', 'background:#00E5FF;color:#062A30;font-family:monospace;border-radius:3px', '— type portfolio.help()') and define window.portfolio = { help(){...}, resume(){ location.href='/Ramu_Roy_Resume.pdf' }, contact(){ return 'royramu694429@gmail.com' } } guarded so it never throws. Cross-link: portfolio.help() mentions the backtick terminal shortcut. ~25 lines total.
